metadata.title: 2022 Akwa Ibom State Public Service Rules

questions.question: According to Rule 010101, who bears the primary responsibility for becoming familiar with the Public Service Rules and extant circulars?
questions.explanation: Rule 010101 makes it the personal responsibility of every officer to acquaint himself or herself with the Public Service Rules, other regulations, and extant circulars.

questions.question: The Public Service Rules do not apply where they conflict with:
options: Specific terms approved and written into the contract of employment or letter of appointment
questions.explanation: The Rules yield where they conflict with approved written contractual terms or constitutional provisions.

questions.question: The six-digit coding system used in the Public Service Rules represents:
questions.explanation: The first two digits represent the Chapter, the next two the Section, and the last two the Rule Number.

questions.question: Under the Rules, a child adopted by an officer is recognized as the officer's child only when the adoption is:
options: Made in accordance with a statutory provision
questions.explanation: Rule 010103 includes a child adopted in accordance with any statutory provision.

questions.question: A Junior Officer in the Akwa Ibom State Public Service is one appointed on:
questions.explanation: Junior Officers are staff appointed on Grade Level 06 and below.

questions.question: Senior Posts are classified as those on:
questions.explanation: Senior Posts are those graded on Salary Grade Level 07 and above.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT included in the definition of "Electronic Gadgets" under the Rules?
questions.explanation: The Rules list items such as mobile phones, computers, flash drives, scanners and calculators, but not typewriters.

questions.question: Interdiction differs from suspension because interdiction:
options: Is imposed only by the Governor
questions.explanation: Interdiction places an officer on half salary pending investigation or criminal proceedings.

questions.question: Suspension under the Rules generally entails:
options: Temporary stay off duty without payment of salary
questions.explanation: Suspension keeps an officer away from duty without payment of salary and is distinct from interdiction.

questions.question: Subsequent amendments to the Public Service Rules shall be effected through:
questions.explanation: Rule 010107 provides that subsequent amendments shall be made through relevant circulars only.

questions.question: Appointments to all posts in the State Civil/Public Service are made on the authority of:
options: The State Civil Service Commission or any other such body
questions.explanation: Rule 020101 vests appointment authority in the State Civil Service Commission or any other authorized body.

questions.question: Appointments to posts on GL 07 and above shall normally be made:
questions.explanation: Rule 020102 requires vacancies and advertisements for senior posts.

questions.question: When appointing officers to senior posts, appointments should, as much as possible, reflect:
questions.explanation: The Rules require appointments to senior posts to reflect the state character as much as possible.

questions.question: If a candidate accepts a position lower than the one originally applied for, the officer shall NOT:
options: Petition for upgrading based on comparison with colleagues
questions.explanation: Rule 020102 prohibits such petitions after assumption of duty.

questions.question: Appointments into posts on GL 06 and below are handled by:
options: The Junior Staff Committee of the Ministry/Department/Agency
questions.explanation: Rule 020103 assigns responsibility to the Junior Staff Committee, subject to the required representation and approval.

questions.question: A meeting of the Junior Staff Committee held without an observer from the State Civil Service Commission shall be:
questions.explanation: The Rules expressly state that such a meeting is null and void.

questions.question: An officer qualifies for an annual increment only after spending at least:
options: Three months on the grade level
Six months on the grade level with good performance
Nine months on the grade level
One year on the grade level
questions.explanation: Rule 020105 requires at least six months on the grade level with good performance.

questions.question: Seniority in a Ministry is determined by:
options: Date of resumption of duty certified by an authorized officer
questions.explanation: Rule 020106 bases seniority on the certified date of resumption of duty.

questions.question: Employing a staff into the Public Service without complying with Rules 020101–020103 constitutes:
questions.explanation: Unauthorized employment contrary to these rules is expressly classified as serious misconduct.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT listed as an eligibility requirement for appointment into the Akwa Ibom State Public Service?
options: Possession of a National Identification Number (NIN)
Medical fitness certified by a Government Medical Officer
Nigerian citizenship as defined by the Constitution
Membership of a recognized professional association in all cases
questions.explanation: The Rules require citizenship, NIN, certificate of origin, age, prescribed qualifications, medical fitness, and a testimonial of good conduct. Membership of a professional association is not listed as a universal requirement.

questions.question: An applicant for appointment into the Akwa Ibom State Public Service must generally be within what age bracket?
questions.explanation: Rule 020205 provides that every applicant must not be less than 18 years and not more than 50 years of age.

questions.question: A candidate seeking appointment into the Public Service must provide a testimonial of good conduct from:
options: The last employer or, if previously unemployed, the last school or college attended
questions.explanation: Rule 020205(f) requires a testimonial of good conduct from the applicant's last employer or last educational institution attended.

questions.question: Recruitment, as defined by the Rules, excludes:
options: Transfer of officers from other public services in the Federation
questions.explanation: Recruitment refers to filling vacancies with persons not already in the Akwa Ibom State Public Service and excludes transfers from other public services within the Federation.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT one of the recognized categories of direct appointment into the Public Service?
options: Appointment as a trainee or pupil
questions.explanation: Rule 020202 recognizes appointment as a trainee/pupil, on probation, or on contract.

questions.question: A trainee appointed to acquire additional professional experience becomes eligible for confirmation only after:
options: Fulfilling the conditions prescribed in the Scheme of Service
Receiving a recommendation from the Permanent Secretary
questions.explanation: Rule 020203 requires trainees to satisfy the conditions laid down in the applicable Scheme of Service before confirmation.

questions.question: Except where otherwise decided by the Civil Service Commission, first appointments into pensionable posts are normally made:
questions.explanation: Rule 020204 provides that first appointments into pensionable establishments are normally on probation.

questions.question: Which of the following documents is specifically required as part of the eligibility criteria for appointment?
questions.explanation: Rule 020205 specifically requires possession of a National Identification Number (NIN).

questions.question: Before appointment into the Public Service, an applicant must be certified medically fit by:
questions.explanation: Rule 020205 requires certification by a Government Medical Officer.

questions.question: Every applicant for government employment must declare all of the following EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Rule 020206 requires declarations regarding criminal convictions, employment history, obligations to current employers, and financial embarrassment—not political party membership.

questions.question: Prior specific approval of the Civil Service Commission is required before appointing a candidate who:
options: Has previously been dismissed from Government Service
questions.explanation: Rule 020206(b) requires prior approval where a candidate has been convicted of a criminal offence or was previously dismissed or retired from Government Service.

questions.question: Applicants for senior posts are required to complete:
questions.explanation: Rule 020207(a) requires applicants for senior posts to complete Form AKC 1.

questions.question: A successful candidate accepting an offer of appointment signifies acceptance using:
questions.explanation: Rule 020207(b) requires the successful candidate to return Form Gen. 75 as acceptance of the offer.

questions.question: Following acceptance of an offer of appointment, the letter of appointment is issued on:
questions.explanation: Rule 020207 provides that the appointment letter is issued on Form Gen. 69C.

questions.question: For pensionable appointments, which form accompanies the appointment documents sent to the Department of Establishments?
questions.explanation: Rule 020207(b)(iv) requires Form Gen. 39 to accompany the documents.

questions.question: Immediately after assuming duty, a newly appointed officer is required to complete:
questions.explanation: Rule 020208 requires every new staff member to enter personal particulars on Form Gen. 39.

questions.question: The Oath of Secrecy for every new appointee is administered using:
questions.explanation: Rule 020209 requires the Oath of Secrecy to be administered using Security Form I.

questions.question: Membership of a secret society by a public servant is prohibited, and failure to renounce such membership constitutes:
questions.explanation: Rule 020211 states that contravention of Rule 020210 is regarded as serious misconduct and may attract dismissal.

questions.question: The normal probationary period before confirmation in service is:
questions.explanation: Rule 020301 provides that officers on probation normally serve two years before confirmation.

questions.question: Under normal circumstances, the probationary period may be reduced to not less than:
questions.explanation: Previous satisfactory public service in cognate posts may reduce the probationary period, but not below six months.

questions.question: Scenario: An officer has already completed two years of probation but has not been confirmed because an extension has been proposed. According to the Rules, such an extension requires the approval of:
options: The Akwa Ibom State Civil Service Commission or other authorized body
questions.explanation: Rule 020301 provides that any extension beyond the normal probationary period must be approved by the Civil Service Commission or other authorized body.

questions.question: An officer on probation is normally required to pass the prescribed examination appropriate to his appointment:
questions.explanation: Rule 020302 requires an officer on probation to pass the prescribed examination appropriate to his appointment during the probationary period.

questions.question: An officer who knowingly makes a false statement in a letter of application for appointment is liable to:
options: Be disqualified or have the appointment terminated if discovered after engagement
Be placed on probation for an additional year
questions.explanation: Any false statement in an application is sufficient for disqualification or termination of appointment if discovered after engagement.

questions.question: The date of birth recorded by an officer at the time of appointment shall:
options: Be changed once every five years
Be maintained throughout the officer's career
Be amended by the Permanent Secretary upon request
questions.explanation: Rule 020109(b) provides that the date of birth recorded at appointment shall remain unchanged throughout the officer's career.

questions.question: Applications for amendment of an officer's personal records must be forwarded to:
questions.explanation: Requests such as change of name, marital status or next-of-kin are forwarded to the Department of Establishments with supporting evidence.

questions.question: Which of the following changes requires documentary evidence before approval?
questions.explanation: Changes to personal records, including change of name, require relevant documentary evidence.

questions.question: Approval for amendment of an officer's personal records issued by any authority other than the Department of Establishments shall:
options: Be valid if endorsed by the Permanent Secretary
questions.explanation: The Rules expressly state that approvals not issued by the Department of Establishments shall not be recognized.

questions.question: Scenario: An officer transfers to another cadre on a higher salary. For seniority purposes, the transfer is treated as:
questions.explanation: Rule 020107 states that transfer to another cadre on a higher salary is treated as a transfer on promotion.

questions.question: Which authority approves appointments into senior posts after eligible candidates have been interviewed?
options: State Civil Service Commission or other authorized body
questions.explanation: Appointments to senior posts are vested in the State Civil Service Commission or another authorized body.

questions.question: A meeting of the Junior Staff Committee held without representation from the State Civil Service Commission is:
options: Valid if attended by the Permanent Secretary
questions.explanation: The Rules specifically declare such meetings null and void.

questions.question: Which officer is responsible for administering the Oath of Secrecy to a newly appointed public servant?
options: The Permanent Secretary or Head of Extra-Ministerial Department/Agency
questions.explanation: Rule 020209 assigns this responsibility to the Permanent Secretary or Head of the Extra-Ministerial Department/Agency.

questions.question: The signed Security Form I should be:
options: Countersigned and preserved by the Permanent Secretary or Head of Department
questions.explanation: The Rules require the completed form to be countersigned and preserved.

questions.question: Which of the following would require prior approval of the Civil Service Commission before appointment?
options: Applicant previously retired from Government Service
Applicant with ten years' private sector experience
questions.explanation: Prior approval is required where an applicant has previously been dismissed or retired from Government Service, or has a criminal conviction.

questions.question: The offer of appointment for a pensionable post is issued on:
questions.explanation: Successful candidates are first issued an offer of appointment on Form Gen. 69 for pensionable appointments before accepting with Form Gen. 75.

questions.question: Which form is used for an offer of appointment to a non-pensionable post?
questions.explanation: Form Gen. 69A is used for offers of non-pensionable appointments.

questions.question: Recruitment into the Public Service primarily refers to:
options: Appointment of persons not already in the Akwa Ibom State Public Service
questions.explanation: Rule 020201 defines recruitment as filling vacancies by appointing persons not already in the Public Service.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a recognized type of direct appointment under Rule 020202?
questions.explanation: Rule 020202 lists trainee/pupil, probation, and contract appointments only.

questions.question: Scenario: An officer's request to change his next-of-kin is approved by his Ministry but not by the Department of Establishments. Under the Rules, the approval is:
questions.explanation: Amendments to personal records are recognized only when approved by the Department of Establishments.

questions.question: The representative of the State Civil Service Commission at a Junior Staff Committee meeting primarily serves to ensure:
options: Compliance with the Public Service Rules during appointments
questions.explanation: Representation from the Commission is required to ensure appointments comply with the Rules and that committee decisions are valid

questions.question: An officer who knowingly continues membership in a secret society after appointment may face:
options: Disciplinary action that may include dismissal
questions.explanation: Contravention of Rule 020210 is serious misconduct and may attract dismissal.

questions.question: Which statement best reflects the purpose of requiring applicants to disclose whether they are under any obligation to remain in their current employment?
options: To determine eligibility for housing allocation
To ensure there are no contractual or legal impediments to taking up the appointment
questions.explanation: Rule 020206 requires applicants to disclose whether they are still under any obligation to remain in current employment so the appointing authority can determine whether they are free to take up the appointment

questions.question: An officer who is due for confirmation at the end of probation will NOT be eligible for confirmation unless he:
options: Has served in at least two Ministries
Has completed probation satisfactorily and passed any prescribed examination
Has attended a foreign training course
Has been promoted at least once
questions.explanation: Confirmation requires satisfactory completion of the probationary period and successful completion of any prescribed examination.

questions.question: The recommendation for confirmation of officers holding senior posts is forwarded to:
options: The Civil Service Commission or other authorized body
questions.explanation: Recommendations concerning confirmation of senior officers are submitted to the Civil Service Commission (or other authorized body) through the prescribed Progress Report and Personal Confidential Forms.

questions.question: A contract appointment differs from a pensionable appointment because it:
options: Is temporary for a specified period and does not provide for pension
Must always last for two years
questions.explanation: Rule 020401 defines a contract appointment as a temporary appointment for a specified period that does not provide for pension benefits.

questions.question: Unless expressly stated in the contract, a contract officer is NOT automatically entitled to:
options: Privileges, emoluments and allowances provided in the Public Service Rules
questions.explanation: The Rules provide that privileges, emoluments and allowances in the Public Service Rules do not apply to contract officers unless specifically included in the contract.

questions.question: Questions regarding the interpretation of a contract affecting a contract officer's conditions of service should be referred to:
questions.explanation: Rule 020402 specifically directs that such questions be referred to the Department of Establishments.

questions.question: Contract appointments may be offered to expatriates only when:
options: The post is on Grade Level 15 and above
questions.explanation: The Rules permit contract appointments for expatriates only where suitable Nigerians are not available.

questions.question: Which Nigerian may legitimately be offered appointment on contract terms?
questions.explanation: Nigerians may be appointed on contract if they are pensioners, over 50 years old at appointment, or specifically request contract employment where it is in the Service's best interest.

questions.question: A Nigerian who is over 50 years old at the time of appointment may be employed:
questions.explanation: Rule 020402(c) expressly provides that Nigerians over 50 years of age may be appointed on contract terms.

questions.question: A non-Nigerian woman married to a Nigerian shall remain on contract until she:
options: Is confirmed by the Civil Service Commission
questions.explanation: Such officers remain on contract until they obtain Nigerian citizenship before consideration for permanent appointment.

questions.question: The duration of a contract appointment is determined by:
options: The period specified in the contract
questions.explanation: Rule 020403 limits the duration of a contract appointment to the period specified in the contract document.

questions.question: Scenario: A Ministry wishes to terminate a contract officer's appointment before expiry of the contract. According to the Rules, the recommendation to the Civil Service Commission should be accompanied by:
options: A full statement explaining the reasons for the recommendation
questions.explanation: The recommendation must be accompanied by a full statement of the considerations leading to the proposed termination.

questions.question: Before deciding to terminate a contract appointment, the Civil Service Commission may:
options: Offer the officer an opportunity to make formal representations
Refer the matter to the Governor
questions.explanation: The Commission may allow the officer to submit formal representations before making a final decision.

questions.question: A contract officer who desires re-engagement should notify Government:
options: At least four months before leave becomes due
questions.explanation: Rule 020405 requires written notification not less than four months before leave is due.

questions.question: If a contract officer fails to notify Government of his desire for re-engagement within the prescribed period, it may be assumed that he:
questions.explanation: In the absence of timely notification, Government may assume the officer does not seek re-engagement.

questions.question: Following a request for re-engagement, the Ministry forwards its recommendation through:
options: The Department of Establishments to the Civil Service Commission
questions.explanation: Recommendations are forwarded through the Department of Establishments to the Civil Service Commission.

questions.question: Which document must accompany a recommendation for re-engagement of a contract officer?
questions.explanation: An up-to-date confidential report must accompany the recommendation unless one has been submitted within the preceding two months.

questions.question: If Government decides not to re-engage a contract officer, the officer should be informed:
options: At the end of his leave
Only after another officer has resumed
questions.explanation: The Rules require that the officer be informed without delay once approval has been obtained.

questions.question: Provided re-engagement is completed before the end of vacation leave, leave granted under the new contract shall be treated as:
options: Continuous with service under the former contract
questions.explanation: Rule 020408 provides that the leave will be treated as continuous with service under the former contract.

questions.question: If a re-engaged contract officer resumes duty before exhausting leave due under the former contract, the unused leave becomes:
questions.explanation: Leave not taken before resumption under the new contract is treated as deferred leave.

questions.question: Scenario: A contract officer is re-engaged to the same office, without a break in service, and on the same salary grade level. What happens to the officer's incremental date?
options: It is reset to the date of the new contract.
It is determined by the Permanent Secretary.
The officer retains the incremental date enjoyed under the former contract.
It is fixed at 1 January of the following year.
questions.explanation: Rule 020410 provides that where a contract officer is re-engaged to the same office without a break in service and on the same salary grade level, the existing incremental date is retained.

questions.question: The permanent release of an officer from one scheduled service to another is known as:
questions.explanation: Rule 020501(a) defines transfer as the permanent release of an officer from one scheduled service to another or from one class to another within the same service.

questions.question: A temporary release of an officer to serve another government or an approved body for a specified period is called:
questions.explanation: Rule 020501(b) defines secondment as the temporary release of an officer to another government or approved body for a specified period.

questions.question: Conversion from one cadre to another is primarily based on:
options: Acquisition of prescribed qualifications and cognate experience
questions.explanation: Rule 020501(c) requires the acquisition of the prescribed qualification and possession of cognate experience.

questions.question: Which process refers to elevating an officer to a higher grade within the same cadre after obtaining additional prescribed qualifications?
questions.explanation: Rule 020501(d) defines upgrading as elevation to a higher grade within the same cadre after obtaining additional qualifications.

questions.question: Advancement means:
options: Elevation to the next grade level as prescribed in the Scheme of Service
Temporary appointment to a higher office
questions.explanation: Rule 020501(e) defines advancement as elevation to the next grade level in accordance with the approved Schemes of Service.

questions.question: Applications for inter-service transfer or secondment to posts on GL. 01–06 are determined by:
options: The State Civil Service Commission only
The Ministry/Extra-Ministerial Department/Agency, subject to the Rules
questions.explanation: Rule 020502(a) vests this responsibility in the Ministry/Extra-Ministerial Department/Agency, subject to clearance by the Head of Civil Service and compliance with the Rules.

questions.question: The Junior Staff Committee handling transfer or secondment of officers on GL. 01–06 acts subject to clearance by the:
questions.explanation: Rule 020502(a) requires clearance by the Head of Civil Service.

questions.question: Applications for inter-service transfer or secondment of officers on GL. 07 and above are determined by:
options: The Akwa Ibom State Civil Service Commission
questions.explanation: Rule 020502(b) places this responsibility on the Akwa Ibom State Civil Service Commission.

questions.question: An application for inter-service transfer of an officer on GL. 07 and above must include confidential reports covering:
options: The last three years (or the whole service if less than three years)
questions.explanation: Rule 020502(b) requires confidential reports covering the last three years of service or the whole service where it is less than three years.

questions.question: Scenario: An officer requests secondment to another government for personal reasons. What is the maximum initial period of such secondment?
questions.explanation: Rule 020502(c) provides that secondment on an officer's own request shall be for a maximum initial period of two years.

questions.question: The total duration of secondment at an officer's request shall not exceed:
questions.explanation: Even after approved extensions, the total period of such secondment must not exceed four years.

questions.question: During secondment at an officer's request, the officer is entitled to:
options: Automatic salary increase every six months
questions.explanation: Rule 020502(c) specifically provides for notional increment during the period of secondment.

questions.question: After returning from secondment, an officer may be granted notional promotion primarily to:
options: Restore seniority affected during the period of absence
questions.explanation: Rule 020502(c) provides for notional promotion to restore the officer's seniority where colleagues were promoted during the secondment period.

questions.question: If an officer is seconded in the public interest, the period of secondment:
questions.explanation: Rule 020502(d) states that secondment in the public interest is not subject to a fixed time limit.

questions.question: During secondment in the public interest, the officer:
options: Continues to hold his substantive post
questions.explanation: The officer continues to hold the substantive post and remains entitled to increment and promotion.

questions.question: Who is responsible for paying the emoluments of an officer on secondment?
questions.explanation: Rule 020502(e) makes the benefiting organization responsible for the officer's emoluments during the secondment.

questions.question: An officer seeking transfer from one senior post to another within the State Civil Service must have served in the original Department for at least:
questions.explanation: Rule 020503(a) requires a minimum of six months' service before seeking transfer.

questions.question: An application for transfer of a senior officer should clearly state:
options: Reasons for the transfer and qualifications for the intended work
questions.explanation: The Rules require applicants to state the reasons for seeking transfer and the qualifications relevant to the work they wish to undertake.

questions.question: Transfers of junior officers from one Department to another may be arranged with:
options: Consent of the officers concerned and the mutual discretion of the relevant Permanent Secretaries/Heads
Approval of the House of Assembly
questions.explanation: Rule 020503(b) allows such transfers with the consent of the officers and the mutual discretion of the relevant Permanent Secretaries/Heads.

questions.question: Scenario: A senior officer wishes to transfer to another Ministry after only four months in the current Department. According to the Public Service Rules, the application should ordinarily be:
options: Approved because the officer is on GL. 10
Declined because the minimum required service period has not been met
questions.explanation: Rule 020503(a) requires an officer to have served a minimum of six months in the original Department before seeking transfer to another Department.

questions.question: Transfer from a non-pensionable appointment to a pensionable appointment requires the approval of:
options: The authority empowered to make the appointment at the relevant level
questions.explanation: Rule 020504(a) provides that transfer from a non-pensionable appointment requires the approval of the authority empowered to appoint at the level concerned.

questions.question: An officer transferring from a non-pensionable appointment to a pensionable appointment should understand that:
options: The appointment may be subject to probation.
Previous salary automatically determines the new salary.
questions.explanation: Such transfers may be subject to a period of probation before confirmation.

questions.question: If an officer transferred from a non-pensionable appointment fails to secure confirmation in the pensionable establishment, the officer:
options: Has no claim to revert to the former appointment, except where specifically provided by the Rules.
Must be transferred to another Ministry.
questions.explanation: Rule 020504(b) states that the officer has no claim to revert except for the specific exception relating to promotion from certain junior posts.

questions.question: The salary of an officer transferring from a non-pensionable appointment to a pensionable appointment is:
options: Not governed by the salary previously received.
questions.explanation: Rule 020504(c) expressly states that previous salary does not determine salary after transfer.

questions.question: An application for transfer to a pensionable appointment from an officer who was over 50 years old when first appointed to a non-pensionable post:
options: Shall be considered after medical examination.
questions.explanation: Rule 020504(d) bars such applications.

questions.question: Serving non-pensionable officers seeking pensionable appointments must undergo medical examination if:
options: Their original appointment was not preceded by a Government Medical Officer's examination.
They have spent five years in service.
questions.explanation: Rule 020505 requires a Government Medical Officer's examination where one was not conducted previously.

questions.question: If a Government Medical Officer certifies such an officer unfit for pensionable employment:
options: Transfer is suspended for one year.
questions.explanation: Rule 020505 clearly provides that the transfer will not be effected.

questions.question: Transfer on promotion to another Ministry may be considered only:
options: In response to an advertised post.
questions.explanation: Rule 020506(a) provides that transfer on promotion shall only be considered in response to an advertised post.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT one of the conditions for transfer under Rule 020506?
options: Qualifications consistent with the Scheme of Service
questions.explanation: Rule 020506 lists service confirmation, qualifications, vacancy and prescribed years in grade—not recommendations by traditional rulers.

questions.question: Before transfer is approved, the contemplated transfer must NOT:
options: Jeopardize the promotion prospects of serving officers.
questions.explanation: Rule 020506(b)(i) protects the promotion prospects of serving officers.

questions.question: Posting officers within a Ministry outside their professional cadres is:
questions.explanation: Rule 020506(c) expressly prohibits posting officers outside their professional cadres.

questions.question: An officer accepted on transfer into the State Civil Service from another Government service shall be placed:
options: On the post normally attained through career progression under the Scheme of Service.
Two grade levels below previous rank.
questions.explanation: Rule 020506(d) provides for placement based on normal career progression under the applicable Scheme of Service.

questions.question: Conversion from one cadre to another is subject to:
questions.explanation: Rule 020507(a) states that conversion is subject to vacancy.

questions.question: Conversion of officers on GL. 06 and below is handled by the:
questions.explanation: Rule 020507(b) assigns this responsibility to the Junior Staff Committee.

questions.question: A meeting considering conversion of junior staff held without an observer from the Civil Service Commission is:
questions.explanation: Rule 020507(b) declares such meetings null and void.

questions.question: Conversion from a sub-professional cadre to a professional cadre is considered by the:
options: Senior Staff Management Committee before approval by the Civil Service Commission.
questions.explanation: Rule 020507(c) requires consideration by the SSMC before approval by the Civil Service Commission.

questions.question: The notional date of conversion is:
options: The date salary is first paid.
The date the officer appears before the Commission with original certificates.
questions.explanation: Rule 020507(d) fixes the notional date as the date the officer appears before the Commission with original certificates.

questions.question: The effective date for remuneration after conversion is:
options: 1st January following the date of conversion.
questions.explanation: Rule 020507(d) provides that remuneration takes effect from 1 January following the date of conversion.

questions.question: Scenario: An officer on GL. 09 acquires a university degree directly related to the officer's current sub-professional cadre. According to the Rules, the officer should ordinarily:
options: Transfer laterally into the full professional cadre.
questions.explanation: Officers on GL. 08–12 in sub-professional cadres who obtain relevant university degrees or approved professional qualifications transfer laterally to the corresponding full professional cadre.

questions.question: Scenario: A GL. 14 officer acquires a university degree related to the officer's present cadre. Unless the approved Scheme of Service provides otherwise, the officer should transfer:
options: To the same grade level in the professional cadre.
To one grade level below the current salary grade level in the full professional cadre.
questions.explanation: Rule 020507(g) provides that officers on GL. 13 and above transfer to one grade level below their existing salary grade level in the corresponding professional cadre, unless otherwise disallowed by the approved Scheme of Service.

questions.question: Upgrading of an officer is primarily intended to:
options: Elevate an officer within the same cadre after acquiring prescribed qualifications
Transfer an officer to another Ministry
questions.explanation: Upgrading refers to elevation within the same cadre after the acquisition of prescribed qualifications in accordance with the approved Scheme of Service.

questions.question: Before an officer can be considered for upgrading, there must ordinarily be:
options: A recommendation from a traditional ruler
An available vacancy and compliance with the approved Scheme of Service
Approval by the State Executive Council
questions.explanation: Upgrading is subject to the availability of a vacancy and compliance with the relevant Scheme of Service.

questions.question: Advancement differs from promotion because advancement:
options: Moves an officer into another cadre
Is elevation to the next grade level as prescribed in the Scheme of Service
questions.explanation: Advancement is movement to the next grade level within the framework prescribed by the approved Scheme of Service.

questions.question: An officer cannot properly benefit from advancement unless:
options: The conditions prescribed in the approved Scheme of Service have been satisfied
The officer has reached 50 years of age
questions.explanation: Advancement is governed by the conditions laid down in the approved Scheme of Service.

questions.question: Which statement best reflects the philosophy of promotion in the Civil Service?
options: Promotion is based solely on seniority.
Promotion is automatic after three years.
Promotion recognizes increased efficiency, merit, and ability.
Promotion depends mainly on political recommendation.
questions.explanation: Rule 020601 establishes that promotion is based on merit, demonstrated efficiency, and ability, not automatic entitlement.

questions.question: Promotion should generally be made:
questions.explanation: Promotions are normally made into existing vacancies in accordance with the Rules and the approved establishment.

questions.question: Which factor should carry the greatest weight when promotion candidates are being assessed?
questions.explanation: Merit and demonstrated ability remain the principal considerations in promotion decisions.

questions.question: Scenario: Two officers satisfy the minimum years in grade. One consistently receives outstanding performance reports, while the other merely meets expectations. Under the Rules, promotion should ordinarily favour:
options: The officer with stronger merit and performance
The officer with longer leave balance
questions.explanation: Where officers are eligible, merit and demonstrated efficiency are major determinants of promotion.

questions.question: An officer who merely completes the prescribed years on a grade level:
options: Acquires an absolute right to promotion.
Becomes eligible for consideration but not entitled to promotion.
questions.explanation: Completing the minimum period makes an officer eligible for consideration; promotion is not automatic.

questions.question: One important source of evidence used in assessing promotion candidates is:
questions.explanation: Performance reports form an important basis for evaluating an officer's suitability for promotion.

questions.question: Which of the following would be inconsistent with the promotion principles in the Rules?
options: Promoting every eligible officer regardless of performance
questions.explanation: Eligibility alone does not guarantee promotion; merit and performance remain essential considerations.

questions.question: Scenario: A vacancy exists, but no eligible officer demonstrates satisfactory merit. According to the spirit of the Rules, the vacancy should:
options: Automatically be filled by the most senior officer.
Be filled only by a candidate who satisfies the promotion requirements.
questions.explanation: Promotion should reflect merit and competence rather than simply filling vacancies regardless of suitability.

questions.question: Promotion is intended primarily to recognize:
questions.explanation: Promotion reflects an officer's demonstrated capacity to assume higher responsibilities efficiently.

questions.question: Which combination best supports an officer's promotion?
options: Merit, efficiency, ability, and satisfactory performance
questions.explanation: The Rules emphasize a combination of merit, efficiency, and ability in assessing promotion.

questions.question: Promotion decisions should be consistent with:
options: Approved establishment and applicable Public Service Rules
questions.explanation: Promotions must comply with the approved establishment and the governing Rules.

questions.question: Scenario: An officer argues that having spent the required number of years on a grade level automatically entitles him to promotion. The correct response is that:
options: Promotion is automatic once time requirements are met.
Time in grade creates eligibility, not an automatic entitlement.
questions.explanation: Time in grade is one condition for eligibility; promotion still depends on merit and other prescribed requirements.

questions.question: The Public Service Rules seek to ensure that promotion:
options: Maintains efficiency within the Civil Service
questions.explanation: Promotion policies are designed to maintain an efficient, competent, and productive Civil Service.

questions.question: Which officer is more likely to receive promotion?
options: One with repeated poor performance reports
One who satisfies the minimum requirements and consistently demonstrates excellent performance
questions.explanation: Consistent high performance and merit strongly support promotion under the Rules.

questions.question: A promotion exercise conducted without regard to merit would be:
options: Consistent with the Public Service Rules
Contrary to the principles governing promotion
questions.explanation: Merit is a fundamental principle governing promotion decisions under the Rules.

questions.question: Scenario: Three officers qualify for promotion. All satisfy the minimum years in grade, but only one consistently demonstrates exceptional efficiency, leadership, and excellent performance reports. Under the Public Service Rules, that officer should ordinarily be:
options: Deferred because the others are more senior.
Considered the strongest candidate for promotion based on merit.
Promoted only after every eligible officer has been promoted.
Required to wait until the next promotion exercise.
questions.explanation: The Rules emphasize merit, efficiency, and ability as the primary criteria for promotion once eligibility requirements have been met.

questions.question: Promotion in the Civil Service should primarily recognize an officer's:
options: Merit, efficiency, and ability to undertake higher responsibilities
questions.explanation: The Rules emphasize that promotion should reward demonstrated merit, efficiency, and the capacity to perform effectively at a higher level.

questions.question: Which of the following is the best indicator that an officer is ready for promotion?
options: Completion of the minimum period on grade level alone
Outstanding performance combined with fulfillment of prescribed requirements
Long service without regard to performance
questions.explanation: Time in grade creates eligibility, but promotion depends on merit, performance, and satisfaction of the prescribed conditions.

questions.question: An officer who consistently receives poor Annual Performance Evaluation Reports should ordinarily:
options: Be considered unsuitable for promotion until performance improves.
questions.explanation: Promotion is based on satisfactory performance and demonstrated competence.

questions.question: A vacancy exists, but none of the eligible officers satisfies the prescribed promotion requirements. The proper action is to:
options: Withhold promotion until a suitable officer is available.
questions.explanation: A vacancy alone does not justify promotion. The officer selected must satisfy the requirements laid down in the Rules.

questions.question: The main purpose of requiring Annual Performance Evaluation Reports during promotion exercises is to:
options: Objectively assess work performance over time.
questions.explanation: Performance reports provide objective evidence of an officer's efficiency, competence, and suitability for higher responsibility.

questions.question: Scenario: Two officers have identical qualifications and years on grade level. One has consistently demonstrated leadership, initiative, and excellent work output. Under the Rules, promotion should ordinarily favour:
options: The officer with the longer surname.
The officer with superior merit and performance.
The officer who joined the Ministry first, regardless of performance.
questions.explanation: Merit remains the decisive consideration where officers are otherwise equally qualified.

questions.question: Which statement about promotion is correct?
options: Promotion is a right once the minimum years have been completed.
Promotion is earned through demonstrated merit and fulfillment of prescribed requirements.
Promotion depends only on academic qualifications.
Promotion is based solely on seniority.
questions.explanation: Completion of minimum years only qualifies an officer for consideration; promotion itself is not automatic.

questions.question: The Civil Service promotion system is designed to ensure that:
options: Every officer reaches the highest grade before retirement.
Only officers who can effectively discharge higher responsibilities advance.
Promotions occur at fixed calendar intervals.
questions.explanation: Promotion aims to maintain an efficient and competent Civil Service.

questions.question: Which of the following would weaken the integrity of a promotion exercise?
questions.explanation: Ignoring documented performance undermines the merit principle established by the Rules.

questions.question: An officer who satisfies all promotion requirements except satisfactory performance reports should ordinarily:
options: Await improvement in performance before promotion.
questions.explanation: Performance remains a fundamental factor in determining suitability for promotion.

questions.question: Promotion to a higher grade level normally carries:
questions.explanation: Promotion reflects confidence that an officer can successfully undertake greater responsibilities.

questions.question: The objective of promotion based on merit is to:
options: Improve efficiency within the Civil Service.
questions.explanation: Merit-based promotion strengthens institutional efficiency and service delivery.

questions.question: Scenario: An officer argues that outstanding academic qualifications alone should guarantee promotion. According to the Rules, the strongest response is:
options: Qualifications must be considered together with merit, efficiency, and other prescribed requirements.
questions.explanation: Academic qualifications are important but do not replace the broader promotion criteria.

questions.question: Which factor best demonstrates an officer's readiness for higher responsibility?
questions.explanation: Consistent high performance provides evidence that the officer can successfully assume greater responsibility.

questions.question: Promotion should contribute directly to:
questions.explanation: The Rules seek to maintain an effective and efficient Civil Service through merit-based advancement.

questions.question: An officer's Annual Performance Evaluation Report primarily measures:
questions.explanation: Performance evaluation provides structured evidence of work quality, conduct, and efficiency.

questions.question: Which principle is least consistent with the Public Service Rules on promotion?
questions.explanation: The Rules reject automatic promotion without regard to merit and performance.

questions.question: Scenario: During a promotion interview, an officer demonstrates exceptional technical knowledge but has several years of unsatisfactory performance reports. Which record should carry significant weight?
options: Annual Performance Evaluation Reports together with the overall assessment.
questions.explanation: Promotion decisions should consider sustained performance rather than a single strong interview.

questions.question: Promotion exercises should inspire officers to:
options: Improve their competence and work performance.
questions.explanation: Merit-based promotion encourages continuous professional improvement.

questions.question: Scenario: Four officers are eligible for promotion. One consistently exceeds performance targets, mentors’ junior officers, demonstrates integrity, and satisfies every prescribed requirement. Applying the principles of the Public Service Rules, this officer should ordinarily:
options: Be regarded as the strongest candidate for promotion.
Wait until all other eligible officers are promoted.
Be promoted only if the oldest among the candidates.
questions.explanation: The promotion provisions are intended to reward sustained merit, efficiency, integrity, and demonstrated ability to undertake higher responsibilities.

questions.question: The responsibility for making promotions in the Akwa Ibom State Public Service is vested in:
options: The State Civil Service Commission or Ministries/Extra-Ministerial Departments/Agencies, as authorized
The Head of Civil Service only
questions.explanation: Rule 020601(a) vests promotion authority in the State Civil Service Commission or Ministries/Extra-Ministerial Departments/Agencies, as applicable.

questions.question: The Junior Staff Committee (JSC) is responsible for handling the appointment, promotion, and discipline of officers on:
questions.explanation: The JSC handles appointment, promotion, and discipline for officers on Grade Levels 01–06.

questions.question: The Chairman of the Junior Staff Committee is the:
questions.explanation: Rule 020601(b)(i) provides that the Director of Administration and Supplies serves as Chairman of the JSC.

questions.question: Members of the Junior Staff Committee, other than the Chairman, shall ordinarily not be below:
questions.explanation: Members of the JSC must not be below Grade Level 08.

questions.question: The quorum for a meeting of the Junior Staff Committee is:
questions.explanation: Rule 020601(b)(i) fixes the quorum at five members, including the Chairman.

questions.question: Which officials must be present as observers during meetings of the Junior Staff Committee?
options: Civil Service Commission and General Services Office
Governor's Office and Ministry of Finance
questions.explanation: Observers from the Civil Service Commission and the General Services Office (GSO) must attend JSC meetings.

questions.question: The Senior Staff Management Committee (SSMC) is chaired by the:
questions.explanation: The Permanent Secretary serves as Chairman of the SSMC.

questions.question: The Member/Secretary of the Senior Staff Management Committee is the:
questions.explanation: Rule 020601(b)(ii) designates the Director of Administration and Supplies as Member/Secretary.

questions.question: Recommendations made by the Senior Staff Management Committee are forwarded to:
options: The Civil Service Commission for determination
questions.explanation: The SSMC makes recommendations which are forwarded to the Civil Service Commission for determination.

questions.question: An officer who is due for promotion but is currently under disciplinary action should ordinarily:
options: Be promoted if a vacancy exists.
Be considered only after the disciplinary matter is resolved.
questions.explanation: Officers due for promotion are to be considered after screening except those who are under disciplinary action.

questions.question: The minimum period an officer on GL. 01–06 must spend on a post before being eligible for promotion is:
questions.explanation: Officers on GL. 01–06 require a minimum of two years before becoming eligible for promotion.

questions.question: The minimum period an officer on GL. 07–14 must spend on a post before promotion eligibility is:
questions.explanation: Officers on GL. 07–14 require a minimum of three years on the post.

questions.question: An officer on GL. 15 and above ordinarily becomes eligible for promotion after serving at least:
questions.explanation: Rule 020601(c) prescribes a minimum of four years for officers on GL. 15 and above.

questions.question: Promotions in the Public Service shall be made strictly on the basis of:
questions.explanation: Rule 020601(d) states that promotions shall be made strictly on the basis of competitive merit among eligible candidates.

questions.question: When assessing the merit of officers for promotion, a distinction should be made between:
options: Performance in the lower grade and potential to perform in the higher post
questions.explanation: The Rules distinguish between an officer's performance in the lower grade and the officer's ability and competence to perform at the higher level.

questions.question: Where two candidates have equal promotion potential, the deciding factors include:
questions.explanation: Where candidates have equal potential, seniority and previous performance records are taken into account.

questions.question: Regardless of merit and seniority, promotion also requires:
options: A generally satisfactory record of conduct
questions.explanation: The Rules require that a generally satisfactory record of conduct be considered in all promotion cases.

questions.question: Responsibility for promoting officers on GL. 07 and above rests with:
options: The State Civil Service Commission after screening by the Ministry or relevant pool office
questions.explanation: Promotions on GL. 07 and above are made by the Civil Service Commission after screening by the Ministry or relevant pool office.

questions.question: Scenario: Two officers on GL. 12 satisfy the minimum years in post and perform equally well in the promotion assessment. One has a stronger previous performance record and greater seniority. According to the Rules, who should ordinarily have the advantage?
options: The more senior officer with the stronger previous record
The officer with more leave days
questions.explanation: Where candidates have equal promotion potential, seniority and previous performance records become deciding factors.

questions.question: Scenario: A Ministry screens all eligible officers for promotion. One officer performs exceptionally well but is currently facing disciplinary proceedings. Applying the Public Service Rules, the Ministry should:
options: Recommend the officer immediately because of outstanding performance.
Consider the officer only after the disciplinary matter has been resolved.
Promote the officer subject to future review.
questions.explanation: Officers who are under disciplinary action are excluded from consideration during the promotion exercise until the disciplinary issue is resolved.

questions.question: Before a non-pensionable officer may be promoted to a pensionable office, the officer must:
options: Be certified medically fit by a Government Medical Officer where no previous government medical examination was conducted.
questions.explanation: Rule 020602 requires a Government Medical Officer to certify the officer medically fit where the earlier non-pensionable appointment was not preceded by such an examination.

questions.question: Before each promotion exercise, the responsible authority shall first:
options: Compile a list of all eligible candidates based on job requirements and established criteria.
questions.explanation: Rule 020603(a) requires the responsible authority to compile a list of all eligible candidates before each promotion exercise.

questions.question: The list of promotion candidates should be compiled primarily on the basis of:
options: Job requirements and previously established criteria.
questions.explanation: The Rules require eligibility lists to be prepared using the job requirements and predetermined assessment criteria.

questions.question: An officer shall not be denied promotion solely because the officer lacks:
options: A formal educational qualification beyond that required for the officer's grade and mode of entry.
questions.explanation: Rule 020603(b) provides that an officer shall not be debarred solely for lacking educational qualifications beyond those required for the grade and mode of entry.

questions.question: Despite Rule 020603(b), an officer cannot be promoted to a post requiring:
options: Formal professional or technological qualifications the officer does not possess.
More than ten years in service.
questions.explanation: The Rule expressly prohibits promotion to posts requiring professional or technological qualifications the officer does not possess, or where the prescribed compulsory examination has not been passed.

questions.question: Which category of officers is required to pass a written examination and/or other prescribed assessment for promotion?
questions.explanation: Rule 020603(c) requires officers on GL. 06–16 to pass a written examination and/or any other prescribed form of assessment.

questions.question: A Ministry may advertise a vacant promotional post only where:
options: Internal candidates are considered unsuitable in very exceptional circumstances.
The vacancy has existed for six months.
The Governor directs that all vacancies be advertised.
questions.explanation: Rule 020603(d) permits advertisement only in very exceptional cases where available officers within the State Civil Service are unsuitable.

questions.question: When officers from other Civil Services are recruited or transferred on promotion into the State Civil Service, they must:
options: Meet the specific job requirements for the post.
Serve an additional probation regardless of status.
questions.explanation: Rule 020603(d) requires such officers to meet the specific job requirements for the posts.

questions.question: Scenario: An officer satisfies every promotion requirement but lacks a university degree that is not required for the officer's current grade or mode of entry. According to the Rules, the officer should:
options: Wait until the degree is obtained.
questions.explanation: The Rules prohibit disqualification solely because an officer lacks additional educational qualifications beyond those prescribed for the grade and mode of entry.

questions.question: Scenario: An officer seeks promotion to a professional post that legally requires registration and a prescribed professional qualification, but the officer lacks both. The proper decision is to:
options: Promote the officer because of seniority.
Promote the officer subject to future registration.
Decline the promotion because the prescribed qualification is absent.
Ignore the qualification requirement if performance is excellent.
questions.explanation: Rule 020603(b) does not permit promotion where the officer lacks mandatory professional or technological qualifications.

questions.question: The purpose of compiling an eligibility list before promotion is primarily to ensure:
options: Fair and structured consideration of all eligible officers.
questions.explanation: Preparing the eligibility list ensures that all officers meeting the prescribed criteria are considered objectively.

questions.question: Which statement best reflects the Rules regarding educational qualifications and promotion?
options: Every promotion requires a university degree.
Only qualifications prescribed for the relevant post are mandatory.
questions.explanation: The Rules distinguish between qualifications required for the post and additional qualifications that are not mandatory.

questions.question: A written promotion examination for officers on GL. 06–16 is intended primarily to:
options: Assess competence using prescribed evaluation methods.
questions.explanation: Rule 020603(c) requires written examinations and/or other assessments as part of evaluating officers for promotion.

questions.question: External recruitment to fill a promotional vacancy should be regarded as:
options: A measure used only in exceptional situations.
questions.explanation: The Rules make clear that advertising promotional vacancies externally is an exceptional measure, not the norm.

questions.question: Scenario: During a promotion exercise, the responsible authority intentionally omits several officers who satisfy all published eligibility requirements. This action would be inconsistent with Rule 020603 because:
options: Eligible candidates should first be compiled into the promotion list.
questions.explanation: Rule 020603(a) requires the compilation of all eligible candidates before the exercise begins.

questions.question: Which of the following best preserves transparency in promotion exercises?
options: Compiling eligibility lists based on established job requirements.
Promoting only officers recommended by supervisors.
questions.explanation: The Rules require objective, predetermined criteria tied to the requirements of the post.

questions.question: An officer on GL. 10 who refuses to participate in the prescribed written promotion assessment should ordinarily:
options: Be promoted because the officer is already eligible.
Be considered to have failed to satisfy a required promotion condition.
questions.explanation: Officers on GL. 06–16 are required to pass the prescribed written examination and/or assessment before promotion.

questions.question: Scenario: A vacancy exists, but the Ministry determines that none of its officers possesses the competence required for the post. According to the Rules, the Ministry may:
options: Promote the most senior officer regardless of competence.
Advertise the post in exceptional circumstances.
questions.explanation: Rule 020603(d) permits external advertisement where available officers are not suitable for promotion.

questions.question: Which principle is most evident in Rules 020601–020603?
options: Promotion should balance fairness with competence.
Promotion is determined solely by years of service.
questions.explanation: These Rules combine eligibility, competitive merit, conduct, qualifications, and objective assessment to promote fairness while ensuring competence.

questions.question: Scenario: During a promotion exercise for GL. 12 officers, four candidates satisfy the minimum years in post. One candidate has an excellent APER record, passes the written assessment, possesses all prescribed qualifications, maintains a satisfactory conduct record, and demonstrates strong potential for higher responsibility. Applying Rules 020601–020603, this candidate should ordinarily:
options: Be regarded as the strongest candidate for promotion on competitive merit.
Wait until every senior officer has been promoted.
Be considered only if no other officer applies.
Be promoted solely because of years in service.
questions.explanation: The Rules require promotion to be based on competitive merit, supported by performance, conduct, qualifications, and successful completion of prescribed assessments.

questions.question: A promotion exercise should primarily be guided by:
options: Established job requirements and approved promotion criteria
questions.explanation: Promotion exercises are based on predetermined job requirements and established criteria to ensure fairness and merit.

questions.question: An officer who possesses outstanding performance records but fails the prescribed compulsory promotion examination should ordinarily:
options: Be promoted because of excellent performance.
Not be promoted until the prescribed examination requirement is satisfied.
questions.explanation: Where a compulsory examination is prescribed, promotion cannot be granted until the officer satisfies that requirement.

questions.question: The requirement for competitive merit in promotion is intended mainly to:
options: Ensure the most suitable eligible officers are selected.
Reduce the number of promotion exercises.
Guarantee equal promotion opportunities regardless of performance.
questions.explanation: Competitive merit ensures that promotion is awarded to the most competent eligible officers based on established criteria.

questions.question: An officer who lacks qualifications not prescribed for the post should:
options: Remain eligible if all prescribed requirements are met.
questions.explanation: Officers are not to be debarred merely because they lack qualifications beyond those prescribed for their grade and mode of entry.

questions.question: The phrase "competitive merit" implies that promotion candidates are:
options: Assessed against one another using approved standards.
questions.explanation: Competitive merit requires comparison of eligible officers using established promotion criteria.

questions.question: Scenario: A GL. 09 officer has served three years, possesses satisfactory conduct, and performs excellently but refuses to sit for the prescribed written assessment. The appropriate decision is to:
options: Promote the officer because of experience.
Defer promotion until the assessment requirement is met.
questions.explanation: Officers on GL. 06–16 are required to pass the prescribed written examination and/or assessment before promotion.

questions.question: Which of the following best reflects fairness in promotion?
options: Applying previously established promotion criteria to all eligible candidates.
Promoting only officers with university degrees.
Promoting officers recommended by supervisors alone.
questions.explanation: Fairness requires that all eligible officers be assessed against the same established criteria.

questions.question: Where a promotional vacancy is advertised externally, this should ordinarily indicate that:
options: Available officers within the State Civil Service were not considered suitable.
questions.explanation: External advertisement is permitted only in exceptional circumstances where suitable internal candidates are unavailable.

questions.question: An officer's previous performance record becomes especially important when:
questions.explanation: Previous performance records are used to distinguish between candidates with equal promotion potential.

questions.question: Promotion criteria should be established:
questions.explanation: Rule 020603(a) requires promotion criteria to be established before compiling the eligibility list.

questions.question: A Ministry intentionally ignores the established promotion criteria in favour of personal preference. Such action is:
options: Contrary to the promotion procedure prescribed by the Rules.
questions.explanation: Promotion must follow established job requirements and approved criteria rather than subjective preferences

questions.question: The prescribed written assessment for promotion primarily serves to:
options: Objectively assess competence for higher responsibilities.
questions.explanation: The written examination complements other promotion criteria by objectively assessing competence.

questions.question: Scenario: An officer satisfies every promotion requirement except maintaining a satisfactory record of conduct. Applying the Rules, the officer should:
options: Be promoted because performance outweighs conduct.
Be considered unsuitable until the conduct requirement is satisfied.
questions.explanation: A generally satisfactory record of conduct is one of the factors that must be considered in every promotion case.

questions.question: Promotion procedures seek to balance:
options: Merit, conduct, qualifications, and objective assessment.
questions.explanation: The Rules combine several objective factors to ensure competent and fair promotion decisions.

questions.question: Which statement best describes the relationship between eligibility and promotion?
options: Every eligible officer must be promoted.
Eligibility merely qualifies an officer for consideration.
Eligibility guarantees promotion once vacancies exist.
Eligibility removes the need for assessment.
questions.explanation: Eligibility allows an officer to be considered; promotion still depends on competitive merit and satisfaction of all prescribed conditions.

questions.question: Scenario: A promotional post requiring a specific professional licence becomes vacant. The most senior eligible officer lacks the licence, while another candidate possesses it. According to the Rules, the promotion should ordinarily favour:
options: The officer possessing the prescribed professional qualification.
The officer with the longest service.
questions.explanation: An officer may not be promoted to a post requiring professional or technological qualifications that the officer does not possess.

questions.question: The purpose of requiring established promotion criteria before screening candidates is to:
questions.explanation: Predetermined criteria help ensure fairness, transparency, and consistency in promotion decisions.

questions.question: Promotion by competitive merit encourages officers to:
options: Focus only on years of service.
Continuously improve their competence and performance.
questions.explanation: A merit-based system motivates officers to improve their knowledge, skills, and job performance.

questions.question: Scenario: During a promotion exercise, two officers perform equally well in the written assessment. Both satisfy the prescribed qualifications and have satisfactory conduct records. One has consistently stronger APER ratings over several years. Applying the Rules, who should have the advantage?
options: The officer with stronger APER ratings.
The decision should be made by random selection.
questions.explanation: Previous performance records are considered when distinguishing between candidates with equal promotion potential.

questions.question: Scenario: A Ministry proposes to advertise a promotional vacancy externally even though several qualified internal officers satisfy all the prescribed requirements. Under the Public Service Rules, this proposal should ordinarily be:
options: Rejected because external advertisement is reserved for exceptional situations where suitable internal candidates are unavailable.
Approved if the vacancy has existed for more than one month.
Approved only if the post is on GL. 15 and above.
questions.explanation: Rule 020603(d) makes external advertisement an exceptional measure to be used only when suitable internal candidates are not available.

questions.question: Who is authorized to promote officers on Salary Grade Levels 01–06?
options: Ministries/Extra-Ministerial Departments through the Junior Staff Committee
Office of the Head of Civil Service only
questions.explanation: Ministries and Extra-Ministerial Departments/Agencies are authorized to promote officers on GL. 01–06 through their Junior Staff Committee.

questions.question: The primary purpose of convening a meeting of the Junior Staff Committee before promotion is to:
questions.explanation: The Junior Staff Committee screens eligible junior officers before recommendations are made for promotion.

questions.question: A junior officer recommended for promotion to a senior post must ultimately be examined by the:
questions.explanation: Recommendations for promotion from junior to senior posts are examined by the State Civil Service Commission.

questions.question: Who screens officers on senior posts before recommending them for promotion to higher posts?
questions.explanation: Senior officers are screened by the Senior Staff Management Committee before recommendations are forwarded to the Commission.

questions.question: The effective date of promotion shall normally be:
options: 1st January of every year unless otherwise determined.
questions.explanation: Promotions normally take effect from 1st January unless the Commission determines otherwise.

questions.question: Which authority may determine an effective promotion date different from 1st January?
options: The State Civil Service Commission or other authorized body.
questions.explanation: The Rules allow the Commission or other authorized body to determine another effective date.

questions.question: Notional promotion is primarily intended to:
options: Restore an officer's seniority where promotion opportunities were missed for approved reasons.
questions.explanation: Notional promotion restores seniority when an officer misses promotion while absent on approved grounds.

questions.question: Which of the following may qualify an officer for notional promotion?
questions.explanation: Officers on approved in-service training may qualify for notional promotion upon return if found suitable.

questions.question: An officer on approved study leave with pay may be considered for:
questions.explanation: Approved study leave (with or without pay) is one of the grounds for notional promotion.

questions.question: Scenario: An officer missed a promotion exercise because she was on an approved government-sponsored training programme. On returning, she is found suitable for promotion. Which promotion mechanism applies?
questions.explanation: Approved in-service training is one of the recognized grounds for granting notional promotion.

questions.question: When an officer receives notional promotion, he is:
questions.explanation: Notional promotion restores seniority but does not entitle the officer to arrears of salary.

questions.question: Although no salary arrears are paid under notional promotion, the effective date is used to determine:
options: Salary point, future increment, and seniority.
questions.explanation: The effective date determines placement on the salary scale, future incremental date, and seniority.

questions.question: Which officer is not eligible for promotion?
options: A probationary officer satisfying all requirements.
A retired officer re-engaged on contract.
An officer on approved study leave.
questions.explanation: Retired officers re-engaged on contract are not eligible for promotion.

questions.question: An officer appointed directly into the service on contract terms may:
options: Receive automatic promotion after three years.
Be considered only for enhanced appointment during contract renegotiation.
Be promoted through the Junior Staff Committee.
questions.explanation: Contract officers appointed directly into service are not eligible for promotion but may receive enhanced appointments during contract renegotiation.

questions.question: Promotion is generally subject to:
questions.explanation: Promotion depends on available vacancies except where the Scheme of Service provides otherwise.

questions.question: Ministries are required to declare vacancies to the Commission within:
options: Three months after approval of the annual budget.
questions.explanation: Vacancies must be declared within three months of the approval of the annual budget.

questions.question: Failure by a Ministry to declare vacancies within the prescribed period may result in:
questions.explanation: The Rules provide for appropriate sanctions against Ministries that fail to declare vacancies on time.

questions.question: Scenario: A contract officer insists on participating in the annual promotion exercise because he has completed four years of service. According to the Rules, the appropriate response is that:
options: He is eligible because he has served long enough.
He may compete if recommended by his Permanent Secretary.
He is not eligible for promotion while serving on contract.
He may be promoted if he passes the examination.
questions.explanation: Officers appointed on contract terms are not eligible for promotion under the normal promotion system.

questions.question: Scenario: An officer was on approved secondment to another government agency (not in the public interest) and missed a promotion exercise. On returning, she satisfies all promotion requirements. Which is the most appropriate action?
options: Grant notional promotion if found suitable.
questions.explanation: Officers on approved secondment (other than in the public interest) may receive notional promotion upon return if considered suitable.

questions.question: Scenario: A Ministry delays declaring promotion vacancies until eight months after the annual budget is approved, causing the promotion exercise to be delayed. Under the Public Service Rules, this delay:
options: Is acceptable because vacancies may be declared at any time.
Is permitted where promotion examinations have not been conducted.
Contravenes the Rules and may attract sanctions against the Ministry.
Automatically shifts the promotion date to the following year.
questions.explanation: Ministries are required to declare vacancies within three months of budget approval, and failure to do so may attract sanctions.

questions.question: During an officer's probationary period, the appointing authority may terminate the appointment if it is established that the officer:
options: Is not qualified for efficient service.
Has completed one year of service.
questions.explanation: If an officer is found not qualified for efficient service during probation, the appointing authority may terminate the appointment.

questions.question: Where termination during probation is not due to misconduct, the officer should ordinarily receive:
questions.explanation: Where termination is not due to misconduct, it should be effected by one month's notice.

questions.question: An officer whose appointment is terminated during probation because of inefficiency may be granted:
options: Free transport to the place from which he was engaged, provided his conduct was good.
questions.explanation: The Rules provide free transport where the officer's conduct has been good.

questions.question: The refund of training expenses following termination during probation is governed primarily by:
options: The officer's bond relating to such training.
questions.explanation: Any refund of training costs is determined by the bond signed in respect of that training.

questions.question: An officer voluntarily resigns during probation. Government may require the officer to refund:
options: Transportation expenses incurred on the officer's behalf.
questions.explanation: Officers who relinquish appointment during probation may be required to refund transportation costs incurred by Government.

questions.question: An officer who fails to secure confirmation after the probation period may have the appointment:
questions.explanation: Failure to secure confirmation after probation may result in termination in accordance with the Rules.

questions.question: An officer who resigns from the service shall ordinarily:
options: Forfeit all claims to vacation leave.
questions.explanation: An officer who resigns forfeits claims to vacation leave, although any leave granted becomes ex gratia.

questions.question: Any outstanding money owed by a resigning officer to Government shall:
options: Be refunded in full unless waived by Government.
Be transferred to the next employer.
questions.explanation: Outstanding debts must be refunded unless Government exercises its discretion to waive them.
