questions.explanation: Occupants are responsible for Government furniture, cleanliness of the quarters, compound and servants' quarters.

questions.question: Without obtaining approval, an officer removes mosquito-proof fittings and alters the structure of Government quarters. According to the Rules, the officer:
options: Must only notify the maintenance department afterwards.
Is responsible for contravening the Rules governing Government quarters.
Commits no offence if the alterations improve the building.
questions.explanation: Structural alterations or removal of fixtures, including mosquito-proof fittings, require prior approval. The allocated officer is responsible for any contravention.

questions.question: Before vacating Government quarters, an officer must give the officer controlling the quarters at least:
questions.explanation: Officers must give at least forty-eight (48) hours' notice before vacating Government quarters.

questions.question: After moving out of Government quarters, an officer keeps the keys and does not complete the handover documentation. According to the Rules, the officer remains responsible for the quarters until:
options: The authorized representative signs the furniture inventory and key register acknowledging surrender.
questions.explanation: Responsibility for the quarters and Government furniture continues until the authorized representative signs the furniture inventory and key register acknowledging proper handover. Questions 791–800 Chapter 12 – Leave (Part 1: Definitions & General Provisions) Coverage: Rules 120101–120108 – Definitions, Types of Leave, Annual Leave, Deferred Leave, and General Provisions.

questions.question: According to the Public Service Rules, leave is defined as:
options: An officer's absence from work without permission.
The authorized absence of an officer from duty for a specific period as provided in the Rules.
questions.explanation: Leave is defined as the authorized absence of an officer from duty for a specified period under the Rules.

questions.question: A leave address refers to:
options: The address of an officer's office.
A place where the officer can be reached during the leave period.
questions.explanation: A leave address is the location where an officer may be contacted while on leave.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT listed as a type of leave under Rule 120102?
questions.explanation: Jury Leave is not listed among the recognized types of leave in the Public Service Rules.

questions.question: A Permanent Secretary instructs an officer to report to work every morning while on approved annual leave because of staff shortage. According to the Rules, this arrangement is:
options: Permitted if approved by the Permanent Secretary.
Not permitted because annual vacation leave is compulsory and working leave is prohibited.
questions.explanation: Annual vacation leave is compulsory, and officers are not allowed to take "working leave" by reporting for duty during their approved leave period.

questions.question: Where an officer is unable to exhaust annual leave before 31 December due to service exigencies, the leave should ordinarily be exhausted before:
options: 1 February of the following calendar year.
questions.explanation: The Rules allow the officer to complete the leave before 1 February of the following year.

questions.question: The annual leave entitlement for officers on Grade Level 07 and above is:
questions.explanation: Officers on Grade Level 07 and above are entitled to 30 working days of annual leave.

questions.question: An officer on Grade Level 04–06 is entitled to:
questions.explanation: Officers on Grade Levels 04–06 receive 21 working days of annual leave.

questions.question: Before qualifying for another annual leave within a leave-earning year, an officer must ordinarily have served at least:
questions.explanation: An officer qualifies for annual leave after serving not less than six months following the previous leave within the leave-earning service year.

questions.question: Due to an important government assignment, an officer is unable to take part of his annual leave. The Permanent Secretary approves carrying it forward. This leave is known as:
questions.explanation: Deferred leave is leave carried forward because of exceptional circumstances or exigencies of duty with proper approval.

questions.question: Which authority is empowered to approve deferred leave because of exceptional circumstances?
options: The Permanent Secretary or Head of Extra-Ministerial Department/Agency.
questions.explanation: Deferred leave may be approved by the Permanent Secretary or Head of an Extra-Ministerial Department/Agency where justified by exceptional circumstances or service exigencies. Questions 801–810 Chapter 12 – Leave (Part 2: Deferred Leave, Training & Leave Administration) Coverage: Rules 120106–120115 – Deferred Leave, Authority for Leave, Effect of Training, Leave Administration and Temporary Staff.

questions.question: Any annual leave that is not exhausted in accordance with the Public Service Rules shall generally be:
questions.explanation: Vacation leave not exhausted as required by the Rules is deemed forfeited unless properly deferred because of service exigencies.

questions.question: Which of the following officers may be allowed to defer annual leave due to exigencies of service?
options: Officers who simply forgot to apply for leave.
questions.explanation: Officers on special assignments such as tribunals and conferences may be permitted to defer leave because of service exigencies.

questions.question: A Ministry repeatedly prevents an officer from taking annual leave because of operational demands. Under the Rules, the accumulated leave:
options: Must automatically be paid in cash.
Must be converted to casual leave.
questions.explanation: Officers compelled by their Ministries to accumulate leave due to service exigencies may have such leave formally deferred.

questions.question: Deferred leave approved under the Rules should ordinarily be utilized:
options: Before the officer retires from the service.
questions.explanation: Approved deferred leave must be spent before retirement.

questions.question: Authorized deferred leave may be commuted to cash only where:
options: The officer is made to retire prematurely and cannot exhaust the deferred leave before retirement.
The officer has served more than twenty years.
questions.explanation: Cash payment for deferred leave is allowed only where premature retirement makes it impossible to utilize the approved deferred leave.

questions.question: A serving officer voluntarily retires after reaching retirement age and requests payment instead of taking approved deferred leave. According to the Rules, Government should:
options: Pay only half of the leave value.
Decline the request because serving officers are not permitted to commute deferred leave to cash at retirement.
Refer the matter to the Civil Service Commission.
questions.explanation: Serving officers are not allowed to commute deferred leave to cash at retirement except in the specific circumstance of premature retirement provided by the Rules.

questions.question: Authority to approve leave permissible under Chapter 12 for officers under the control of a Ministry rests with:
questions.explanation: Ministries and Extra-Ministerial Departments/Agencies are authorized to approve leave permissible under the Chapter for officers under their control.

questions.question: An officer undergoing in-service training or study leave with pay is entitled during the training period to:
options: Annual leave and leave transport grant.
Neither annual leave nor leave transport grant, but proportionate leave for the remaining part of the leave year.
questions.explanation: Officers on in-service training or study leave with pay are not entitled to annual leave or leave transport grant during training, but qualify for pro-rata leave for the remaining part of the leave year and the full annual leave grant upon resumption.

questions.question: An officer who has been dismissed from the Public Service:
options: Is entitled to annual leave before leaving service.
May receive casual leave after dismissal.
questions.explanation: The Rules expressly provide that officers who are dismissed shall not be granted leave.

questions.question: A Ministry is preparing its leave programme for the following year. According to the Rules, the leave roster should be prepared:
options: At the beginning of the leave year.
During the last quarter of the preceding leave year.
questions.explanation: Ministries and Extra-Ministerial Departments/Agencies are required to prepare leave rosters for the succeeding year during the last quarter of the preceding leave year.

questions.question: Any extension of leave granted under the Public Service Rules shall normally be deducted from:
options: Annual or deferred leave due to the officer.
questions.explanation: Any approved extension of leave is deducted from the officer's vacation/annual or deferred leave entitlement.

questions.question: Special leave without salary may be granted to an officer primarily for the purpose of:
options: Undertaking a course of study likely to enhance the officer's value to Government.
questions.explanation: Special leave without salary may be granted to enable an officer undertake studies that will enhance his usefulness to Government.

questions.question: An officer is recalled to perform official duties during his approved annual leave. According to the Rules, the period spent on duty shall:
options: Be deducted from his leave entitlement.
Be regarded as leave without pay.
Not be counted against his leave entitlement.
questions.explanation: Where an officer performs official duties during vacation leave, that period is not reckoned against the leave entitlement.

questions.question: An officer attending a course of instruction with special conditions shall receive:
options: No leave extension under any circumstance.
Such extension of leave as permitted by the applicable conditions.
questions.explanation: The Rules provide for leave extension where the conditions governing the course permit it.

questions.question: While on annual leave, an officer requests additional leave because of urgent family matters. According to the Rules, the extension may be granted:
options: On full salary until deferred leave is exhausted, and thereafter without salary.
For a maximum of seven days only.
Only if the officer is on Grade Level 15 and above.
questions.explanation: In exceptional cases involving urgent private affairs, leave may be extended on full salary until deferred leave is exhausted and thereafter without salary.

questions.question: An officer outside Nigeria who wishes to apply for an extension of leave should send the application to:
options: The Nigerian Embassy only in Abuja.
questions.explanation: Applications from outside Nigeria should be addressed through the nearest Nigerian Mission.

questions.question: While on leave, every officer must furnish the Ministry or Extra-Ministerial Department/Agency with:
options: The intended leave address or destination.
questions.explanation: Officers spending leave within or outside Nigeria must provide their intended destination or leave address.

questions.question: Casual leave granted within a leave year shall not exceed an aggregate of:
questions.explanation: Casual leave is limited to an aggregate of seven calendar days within a leave year unless special approval is obtained.

questions.question: A Head of Department grants an officer 10 days of casual leave without obtaining approval from the Department of Establishments. According to the Rules, this action is:
options: Proper because Heads of Department may grant any duration.
Proper if the officer has many years of service.
Contrary to the Rules because casual leave exceeding seven days requires specific approval from the Department of Establishments.
Acceptable if the officer is sick.
questions.explanation: Casual leave beyond seven calendar days requires the specific approval of the Department of Establishments.

questions.question: Leave of absence on grounds of public policy shall be approved by:
options: The Department of Establishments on the recommendation of the Permanent Secretary or Head of the officer's Ministry/Department.
questions.explanation: Leave of absence is approved by the Department of Establishments upon the recommendation of the appropriate Permanent Secretary or Head of Extra-Ministerial Department/Agency. Questions 821–830 Chapter 12 – Leave (Part 4: Leave of Absence) Coverage: Rules 120128–120202 – Types of Leave of Absence, Guidelines, Public/Private Interest, Overstay, Annual Leave in Exceptional Cases.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT listed as a type of leave of absence under the Public Service Rules?
options: Leave of absence to join a spouse on a course of instruction abroad.
Leave of absence on grounds of public policy for Technical Aid.
Leave of absence to take up a non-elective political appointment.
Leave of absence to establish a private business.
questions.explanation: The Rules list several categories of leave of absence, but establishing a private business is not one of them.

questions.question: Serving spouses who wish to accompany officers on approved public service postings may be granted:
questions.explanation: Serving spouses accompanying officers on approved public service postings may be granted leave of absence without pay.

questions.question: An officer is granted leave of absence in the public interest. During this period, the leave will ordinarily:
options: Not count for promotion or annual increment.
Count toward promotion, advancement, annual increment and be pensionable.
Automatically qualify the officer for retirement.
questions.explanation: Leave of absence granted in the public interest counts towards promotion, advancement, annual increment and is pensionable, except where spent on non-scheduled service.

questions.question: An officer on approved leave of absence for private purposes is:
options: Entitled to full salary and allowances.
Not entitled to salary or allowances during the period.
Entitled to pension contributions throughout the period.
questions.explanation: Officers on leave of absence for private purposes are not entitled to salary or allowances, and the period is not pensionable.

questions.question: The period of leave of absence granted for private purposes:
options: Counts toward promotion and annual increment.
Does not count toward annual increment, promotion or advancement.
questions.explanation: Leave of absence for private purposes does not count for annual increment, promotion or advancement and is not pensionable.

questions.question: A serving officer applies for leave of absence in order to contest an election into a legislative office. According to the Rules, the application should be:
options: Approved if recommended by the Permanent Secretary.
Refused because leave of absence shall not be granted to participate in elective politics.
questions.explanation: The Rules expressly prohibit granting leave of absence to participate in elective politics.

questions.question: At the expiration of leave of absence, an officer should apply for re-absorption through:
options: His Ministry/Extra-Ministerial Department/Agency to the Department of Establishments.
questions.explanation: Applications for re-absorption are made through the officer's Ministry or Extra-Ministerial Department/Agency to the Department of Establishments.

questions.question: An officer fails to return after the expiration of approved leave of absence without obtaining an extension. Under the Rules, the officer shall be deemed to have:
options: Absented himself from duty without leave or permission.
questions.explanation: Overstaying leave of absence is treated as absence from duty without leave or permission.

questions.question: The normal duration of leave of absence under Rule 120127 is:
options: Four years, subject to extension for another four years.
questions.explanation: Leave of absence is granted for a term of four years and may be extended for another four years.

questions.question: An officer has accumulated annual leave because of exceptional service requirements. Before the deferment can take effect, the Ministry must:
options: Obtain approval from the Department of Establishments.
Obtain approval from the Civil Service Commission.
questions.explanation: Where exceptional circumstances require deferment of annual leave, the matter should be submitted to the Department of Establishments for approval, and any approved deferred leave must be taken before retirement or be forfeited. Questions 831–840 Chapter 12 – Leave (Part 5: Annual Leave Procedures, Recall & Leave Transport Grant) Coverage: Rules 120203–120212 – Leave Procedures, Recall from Leave, Leave Transport Grant and Related Provisions.

questions.question: Before proceeding on annual leave, an officer is expected to:
options: Hand over official duties to another officer as directed.
Lock the office and keep the keys.
Submit all Government property to the Accountant-General.
Obtain approval from the Civil Service Commission.
questions.explanation: Officers are expected to make proper handing-over arrangements before proceeding on leave to ensure continuity of official duties.

questions.question: A Ministry discovers an emergency requiring the immediate services of an officer already on annual leave. Under the Rules, the officer may:
options: Ignore the request until the leave expires.
Be recalled to duty in the public interest.
Resume duty only after obtaining permission from the Civil Service Commission.
questions.explanation: Government reserves the right to recall an officer from leave whenever the exigencies of the service so require.

questions.question: Where an officer is recalled from leave on official grounds, the unused portion of the leave:
options: May be enjoyed at a later date.
questions.explanation: The balance of leave not enjoyed because of an official recall may be taken later in accordance with the Rules.

questions.question: The primary purpose of the Leave Transport Grant is to:
options: Assist an officer with transportation during annual leave.
questions.explanation: Leave Transport Grant is intended to assist officers with transportation expenses associated with annual leave.

questions.question: Leave Transport Grant is normally payable:
options: Once in each leave year in connection with approved annual leave.
questions.explanation: The grant is payable once during a leave year and is tied to approved annual leave.

questions.question: An officer collects Leave Transport Grant but eventually does not proceed on the approved annual leave. According to the Rules, the officer should:
options: Keep the grant since approval had already been given.
Convert it into deferred leave benefits.
questions.explanation: Where leave is not taken after the grant has been paid, the Leave Transport Grant is recoverable in accordance with the Rules.

questions.question: An officer is generally not entitled to receive Leave Transport Grant:
options: More than once in the same leave year.
questions.explanation: The Leave Transport Grant is ordinarily limited to one payment per leave year.

questions.question: After receiving Leave Transport Grant, an officer intentionally submits false travel information to retain the payment without taking leave. Such conduct is best classified as:
options: Acceptable where no complaint is made.
questions.explanation: Obtaining or retaining Government funds through false representations constitutes misconduct and the grant is subject to recovery.

questions.question: An officer recalled from leave because of service exigencies:
options: May resume and complete the outstanding leave when approved.
Must convert the remaining leave to cash.
Automatically receives double Leave Transport Grant.
questions.explanation: The Rules permit an officer recalled from leave to complete the unexpired portion of the leave at an approved time.

questions.question: A Ministry schedules annual leave for all officers to maintain uninterrupted public service. The principal objective of this arrangement is to:
options: Ensure continuity and efficiency of Government operations while officers enjoy their leave entitlements.
Reduce Government expenditure on Leave Transport Grant.
Allow officers to accumulate leave indefinitely.
questions.explanation: Leave administration is organized to balance officers' statutory leave entitlements with the uninterrupted and efficient delivery of public services. Chapter 12 – Leave (Part 6: Examination Leave, Study Leave, Adoption Leave & Paternity Leave) Coverage: Rules 120213–120224 – Examination Leave, Study Leave with Pay, Adoption Leave, Paternity Leave and Related Provisions.

questions.question: An officer may be granted Examination Leave primarily to:
options: Prepare for a private business venture.
Sit for an approved examination relevant to the Public Service.
questions.explanation: Examination Leave is granted to enable an officer prepare for and sit approved examinations that are relevant to the officer's duties or career development in the Public Service.

questions.question: An officer applies for Examination Leave to write a professional examination unrelated to the functions of the Public Service. According to the Rules, the application should ordinarily be:
options: Considered only if the examination is relevant to the Service.
questions.explanation: Examination Leave is intended for approved examinations that are relevant to the officer's service and career progression.

questions.question: Study Leave with pay is generally granted to officers for the purpose of:
options: Pursuing approved courses that will improve their effectiveness in the Public Service.
questions.explanation: Study Leave with pay is granted to enable officers acquire knowledge and skills beneficial to Government service.

questions.question: Which authority is responsible for approving Study Leave with Pay in accordance with the Public Service Rules?
options: The appropriate Government authority as prescribed under the Rules.
questions.explanation: Study Leave with Pay is subject to approval by the competent Government authority in accordance with the Public Service Rules.

questions.question: A female officer legally adopts a child and applies for leave to care for the child. Under the Public Service Rules, she may be granted:
questions.explanation: The Rules recognize Adoption Leave for eligible female officers who legally adopt a child.

questions.question: Adoption Leave under the Public Service Rules is intended primarily to:
options: Enable the officer relocate to another State.
Allow the adopting parent adequate time to bond with and care for the adopted child.
questions.explanation: Adoption Leave provides an eligible officer with time to care for and bond with the adopted child following the adoption process.

questions.question: Paternity Leave is granted to:
options: Every officer regardless of family circumstances.
An eligible male officer whose spouse has delivered a baby or legally adopted a child.
Only officers on Grade Level 14 and above.
Only officers serving in health institutions.
questions.explanation: The Rules provide Paternity Leave for eligible male officers following childbirth or the legal adoption of a child by their spouse.

questions.question: A male officer requests Paternity Leave after the birth of his child. The principal objective of granting the leave is to:
options: Allow him support his spouse and care for the newborn child.
Permit him to proceed on vacation.
questions.explanation: Paternity Leave is intended to enable the officer provide support to his spouse and participate in the care of the newborn or newly adopted child.

questions.question: Which of the following is TRUE regarding Adoption Leave and Paternity Leave?
options: They replace an officer's annual leave entitlement.
They are special categories of leave provided under the Public Service Rules for qualifying officers.
They are granted only after retirement.
They are available only to officers on Grade Level 15 and above.
questions.explanation: Adoption Leave and Paternity Leave are distinct leave categories created for eligible officers and do not replace annual leave.

questions.question: A Human Resource Officer is preparing guidance on the various leave provisions in Chapter 12. Which statement best reflects the overall objective of the Chapter?
options: To discourage officers from taking leave.
To provide a structured framework governing different categories of leave while ensuring efficient service delivery.
To reduce Government expenditure on staff welfare.
To allow Ministries to determine leave rules independently.
questions.explanation: Chapter 12 establishes comprehensive rules governing leave administration while balancing officers' welfare with the uninterrupted and efficient operation of the Public Service. Questions 851–860 Chapter 13 – Free Transport Facilities Coverage: Rules 130101–130108 – Eligibility, Conditions and Administration of Free Transport Facilities.

questions.question: The primary purpose of Free Transport Facilities under the Public Service Rules is to:
options: Assist eligible officers travelling on approved Government business or in circumstances provided by the Rules.
Provide every officer with an official vehicle.
questions.explanation: Free Transport Facilities are provided for eligible officers in circumstances approved under the Rules and are intended to facilitate official service needs.

questions.question: An officer requesting Free Transport Facilities must:
options: Meet the conditions prescribed under the Public Service Rules.
Obtain approval from the Civil Service Commission only.
questions.explanation: Officers must satisfy the prescribed eligibility conditions before Free Transport Facilities may be granted.

questions.question: An officer applies for Government-funded transport for a purely personal holiday. According to the Rules, the request should:
options: Be approved if the officer is on Grade Level 15 and above.
Be declined because Free Transport Facilities are not intended for private holidays.
Be converted into Leave Transport Grant.
questions.explanation: Free Transport Facilities are provided only in circumstances authorized by the Rules and not for private vacations.

questions.question: An officer who knowingly makes a false claim in connection with Free Transport Facilities is liable to:
options: Appropriate disciplinary action under the Public Service Rules.
questions.explanation: False claims relating to Government benefits constitute misconduct and attract disciplinary action.

questions.question: Free Transport Facilities provided by Government should be used:
options: For any journey chosen by the officer.
Strictly for the purpose for which they were approved.
As a substitute for official imprest.
questions.explanation: Transport facilities granted by Government are to be used only for their approved official purpose.

questions.question: After obtaining Government transport approval for official travel, an officer uses the facility for an unrelated private trip. This action is:
options: Acceptable if no extra cost is incurred.
A misuse of Government transport facilities.
Permissible after notifying the Head of Department.
questions.explanation: Government transport benefits must not be diverted to private purposes outside the approved authorization.

questions.question: The administration of Free Transport Facilities should be guided principally by:
options: Economy, accountability and compliance with the Public Service Rules.
questions.explanation: Government transport benefits are administered within the framework of accountability and compliance established by the Rules.

questions.question: A Ministry discovers that an officer received transport benefits through forged documents. The appropriate response under the Rules is to:
options: Ignore the matter if the journey has been completed.
Recover any improper benefit and institute disciplinary measures.
Convert the benefit into Leave Transport Grant.
questions.explanation: Fraudulent claims for Government transport benefits warrant recovery and disciplinary action.

questions.question: The guiding principle behind Chapter 13 is that Government transport benefits should:
options: Be available to every officer without restriction.
Be granted only in accordance with the provisions of the Public Service Rules.
Be determined solely by the Head of Department.
questions.explanation: Eligibility and administration of Free Transport Facilities are governed strictly by the provisions of Chapter 13.

questions.question: An Accounting Officer is reviewing applications for Free Transport Facilities. Which consideration should take priority?
options: Compliance with the eligibility conditions and approval procedures in the Rules.
questions.explanation: Applications should be assessed based on the conditions and procedures prescribed by the Public Service Rules. Questions 861–870 Chapter 14 – Courses of Instruction Coverage: Rules 140101–140205 – Courses of Instruction, Training Responsibilities and Obligations of Officers.

questions.question: The principal objective of Government-sponsored courses of instruction is to:
options: Enable officers to take extended vacations.
Improve officers' knowledge, competence and effectiveness in the Public Service.
questions.explanation: Courses of instruction are intended to enhance officers' capacity and improve service delivery.

questions.question: An officer nominated for an approved course of instruction is expected to:
options: Participate fully and comply with the conditions governing the course.
questions.explanation: Officers nominated for approved courses are expected to attend and comply with all applicable conditions.

questions.question: An officer abandons a Government-sponsored course without valid authorization. According to the Rules, the officer may:
options: Continue to receive all course benefits without consequence.
questions.explanation: Failure to comply with the conditions of Government-sponsored training may attract disciplinary measures.

questions.question: Government-sponsored training should primarily be:
options: Based on the needs of the Public Service.
Limited to officers above Grade Level 14.
questions.explanation: Training opportunities are intended to meet the manpower and development needs of the Public Service.

questions.question: After successfully completing an approved course of instruction, an officer is generally expected to:
options: Apply the acquired knowledge in the performance of official duties.
questions.explanation: The purpose of Government-sponsored training is to improve performance and service delivery.

questions.question: An officer refuses to attend a mandatory Government-approved training programme without reasonable justification. The officer's action is:
options: A breach of the obligations associated with Government-sponsored training.
questions.explanation: Officers are expected to comply with approved training requirements in accordance with the Rules.

questions.question: Responsibility for developing competent manpower within the Public Service is achieved partly through:
questions.explanation: Chapter 14 emphasizes training and capacity development through organized courses of instruction.

questions.question: A Ministry sponsors an officer for specialized professional training. The expected benefit to Government is:
options: Improved institutional capacity and better service delivery.
questions.explanation: Government-sponsored training is intended to improve institutional effectiveness through enhanced staff competence.

questions.question: The success of Government-sponsored courses of instruction depends largely on:
options: Officers faithfully observing the conditions attached to the training.
The officer's length of service alone.
Whether the training is conducted abroad.
The amount of transport allowance paid.
questions.explanation: Compliance with the terms and objectives of approved training ensures the intended benefits are realized.

questions.question: A newly appointed Director asks why Government invests in continuous staff training. Which response best reflects Chapter 14?
options: It is primarily a staff welfare programme.
It equips officers with the knowledge and skills required for improved efficiency, productivity and effective public service delivery.
It exists mainly to reduce annual leave.
It guarantees automatic promotion after every course.
questions.explanation: Chapter 14 emphasizes continuous learning and professional development to improve efficiency and effectiveness in the Public Service. Questions 871–880 Chapter 15 – Allowances (Part 1: Definitions & General Allowances) Coverage: Rules 150101–150108 – Definition, Types of Allowances, Kilometer Allowance, Hotel Accommodation Allowance, Duty Tour Allowance, Estacode and Duty Visits Outside Nigeria.

questions.question: Under Chapter 15, an allowance is defined as:
options: A monetary benefit other than salary granted to an officer for a specific purpose.
Any salary increase approved by Government.
A bonus paid at the end of the year.
questions.explanation: Rule 150101 defines an allowance as a monetary benefit other than salary granted for a specific purpose.

questions.question: Allowances provided under Chapter 15 are generally subject to review every:
questions.explanation: All allowances under Chapter 15 are reviewed every five years through appropriate circulars.

questions.question: Resettlement Allowance is payable where:
options: An officer requests transfer for personal reasons.
An officer's living condition has been disturbed as a result of an approved posting or transfer.
An officer proceeds on annual leave.
An officer purchases a new residence.
questions.explanation: Resettlement Allowance is payable where a posting or transfer disturbs the officer's living condition.

questions.question: A newly appointed officer reports to a duty station several hundred kilometres from home. Which allowance is specifically intended to cover the journey?
questions.explanation: Kilometer Allowance is payable to newly appointed officers reporting to their duty station and in other specified situations.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT listed among the allowances payable under Chapter 15?
questions.explanation: Pension Allowance is not listed among the allowances in Rule 150102.

questions.question: An officer posted to a station outside the officer's town of domicile is entitled to transport fare for:
options: The officer, spouse, and a maximum of four children.
The officer and all dependants without limit.
questions.explanation: Rule 150104 provides transport fare for the officer, spouse, and a maximum of four children.

questions.question: In addition to transport fare, a newly posted officer may receive hotel accommodation for the first:
questions.explanation: Eligible officers may receive hotel accommodation for the first twenty-eight days or an allowance in lieu.

questions.question: An officer embarks on an officially approved inspection tour. Which allowance is specifically intended to cover lodging and feeding expenses?
questions.explanation: Duty Tour Allowance enables officers meet lodging and feeding expenses during approved official tours.

questions.question: Eligibility for Estacode Allowance is subject to approval by:
options: The Head of Civil Service on the recommendation of the Permanent Secretary/Head of MDA.
questions.explanation: Estacode Allowance requires the approval of the Head of Civil Service based on the recommendation of the appropriate Permanent Secretary or Head of an Extra-Ministerial Department/Agency.

questions.question: A Permanent Secretary travelling abroad on official assignment requests Government to arrange accommodation and feeding instead of receiving full estacode. Under the Rules, the officer is entitled to:
questions.explanation: Where Government arranges accommodation and feeding for specified senior officers on official foreign assignments, they are entitled to 25% of their estacode allowance. Questions 881–890 Chapter 15 – Allowances (Part 2: Duty Visits, Resettlement & Teaching Allowances) Coverage: Rules 150108–150302 – Duty Visits Outside Nigeria, Resettlement Allowance and Teaching Allowance.

questions.question: An officer proceeding on an approved duty visit outside Nigeria is ordinarily entitled to:
options: Air passage for the officer only.
Air passage for the officer and the entire family.
questions.explanation: Rule 150108 provides that an officer on duty outside Nigeria is entitled to air passage for himself or herself.

questions.question: Under what condition may an officer's spouse accompany the officer abroad at public expense?
options: When the official assignment lasts not less than nine months.
When the officer is on annual leave.
When the officer is a Permanent Secretary.
questions.explanation: Where the duration of the duty assignment is at least nine months, the spouse may accompany the officer at public expense.

questions.question: An officer incurs transportation expenses that are essential to official business during an overseas assignment. According to the Rules, Government shall:
options: Pay a flat-rate transport allowance only.
questions.explanation: Officers are entitled to reimbursement of actual transportation expenses essential to the official business of the visit.

questions.question: The primary purpose of Resettlement Allowance is to:
options: Compensate an officer for out-of-pocket expenses arising from an approved transfer that are not covered elsewhere.
questions.explanation: Rule 150201 states that Resettlement Allowance compensates officers for transfer-related expenses not covered by other regulations.

questions.question: For the purpose of Chapter 15, which of the following is regarded as a transfer?
options: Transfer from one station to another during a tour of service.
Transfer from one station to another on return from leave.
Secondment from the Service to another Government in the Federation.
questions.explanation: Rule 150202 includes all these circumstances within the meaning of "transfer."

questions.question: Resettlement Allowance is payable at the rate of:
questions.explanation: Rule 150203 fixes Resettlement Allowance at 30% of an officer's annual basic salary.

questions.question: An officer personally requests a transfer from Uyo to Eket for family reasons. Which benefit is the officer entitled to?
questions.explanation: Where the transfer is at the officer's own request, only Transport Allowance is payable; Resettlement Allowance is not.

questions.question: Part-time Teaching Allowance is payable to:
options: Every officer in the Public Service.
Teachers who teach on a part-time basis.
questions.explanation: Rule 150301 provides that Part-time Teaching Allowance is payable to teachers who teach on a part-time basis.

questions.question: The rates for Part-time Teaching Allowance are determined by:
options: Relevant Government circulars, subject to periodic review.
questions.explanation: The rates are prescribed by relevant circulars and are reviewed every five years.

questions.question: An Administrative Officer whose normal duties do not involve teaching is posted to teach full-time at a Government training institution. Under the Rules, the officer:
options: Is not entitled to any teaching-related benefit.
Is entitled to an annual Teaching Allowance approved by Government for the duration of the posting.
questions.explanation: Rule 150302 provides that officers in Professional, Administrative, Executive, Technological and Allied cadres posted to full-time teaching in recognized institutions are entitled to an annual Teaching Allowance during the period of such posting. Questions 891–900 Chapter 15 – Allowances (Part 3: Warm Clothing, Wardrobe & Other Allowances) Coverage: Rules 150401–150505 – Warm Clothing Allowance, Wardrobe Allowance, Other Allowances, Non-Accident Bonus and Domestic Servants.

questions.question: An officer required by Government to proceed to a foreign country on official duty or an approved course of instruction is eligible for a Warm Clothing Allowance of:
questions.explanation: Rule 150401(i) provides that an eligible officer shall receive a Warm Clothing Allowance of US$2,000 once every three years.

questions.question: The Warm Clothing Allowance may ordinarily be received:
questions.explanation: The allowance is specifically limited to once every three years.

questions.question: An officer received Warm Clothing Allowance last year and has been nominated for another official overseas assignment this year. According to the Rules, the officer:
options: Automatically qualifies for another Warm Clothing Allowance.
Qualifies only if travelling to a colder country.
Does not ordinarily qualify because the three-year interval has not elapsed.
questions.explanation: The allowance is payable only once every three years, regardless of the number of qualifying overseas assignments within that period.

questions.question: Wardrobe Allowance is payable at the rate of:
questions.explanation: Rule 150401(ii) fixes Wardrobe Allowance at 10% of the officer's annual basic salary, payable once every year.

questions.question: Wardrobe Allowance is payable:
questions.explanation: The Rule provides for payment once a year.

questions.question: According to Rule 150501, allowances such as rent, transport, books/projects, entertainment, utility, responsibility, shift duty and hazard allowances are payable:
options: At rates fixed permanently in the Public Service Rules.
In accordance with relevant circulars, subject to review every five years.
At the discretion of each Ministry.
Only after approval by the Civil Service Commission.
questions.explanation: These allowances are governed by relevant circulars and are reviewed every five years.

questions.question: A Ministry decides to increase the Hazard Allowance without any Government circular authorizing the change. According to the Rules, this action is:
options: Proper because Ministries may fix allowance rates.
Proper if approved by the Permanent Secretary.
Inconsistent with the Rules because such allowances are governed by relevant circulars.
questions.explanation: Rates for these allowances are determined through relevant Government circulars, not unilateral ministerial decisions.

questions.question: Which category of officers is specifically eligible for the Non-Accident Bonus?
options: All officers who travel on official duty.
Motor Drivers, Driver/Mechanics and Plant Operators who are not involved in any accident during the qualifying period.
questions.explanation: Rule 150502 limits the bonus to Motor Drivers, Driver/Mechanics and Plant Operators who remain accident-free during the qualifying year.

questions.question: A Government driver is found responsible for an accident during the qualifying year. What is the consequence under the Rules?
options: The driver receives half of the Non-Accident Bonus.
The driver forfeits the Non-Accident Bonus.
The driver receives the bonus after six months.
The driver receives the bonus only with the Permanent Secretary's approval.
questions.explanation: Officers in charge of transport must keep accident records, and drivers who are at fault for accidents forfeit the bonus.

questions.question: The Non-Accident Bonus is payable:
options: Only in December, upon presentation of the prescribed Non-Accident Bonus Certificate.
questions.explanation: Rule 150504 provides that the bonus is payable only in December on the strength of a Non-Accident Bonus Certificate issued by the officer in charge of transport. Questions 901–910 Chapter 15 – Allowances (Part 4: Domestic Servants & Integrated Allowance Scenarios) Coverage: Rules 150505–150507 and related provisions on allowances in Chapter 15.

questions.question: The rates of Domestic Servants Allowance payable to eligible officers are prescribed by:
questions.explanation: Domestic Servants Allowance is among the allowances whose rates are prescribed through relevant Government Circulars and reviewed periodically.

questions.question: Allowances such as Rent, Utility, Entertainment and Domestic Servants Allowance are generally:
options: Fixed permanently in the Public Service Rules.
Reviewed every five years through Government Circulars.
questions.explanation: Chapter 15 provides that these allowance rates are governed by Government Circulars and are subject to periodic review every five years.

questions.question: An officer claims both Duty Tour Allowance and full Hotel Accommodation Allowance for the same official assignment, contrary to the approved conditions. The accounts officer should:
options: Pay whichever claim complies with the applicable Rules and approved conditions.
Refer the matter to the Governor.
questions.explanation: Allowances should only be paid in accordance with the applicable provisions and approved conditions. Claims inconsistent with the Rules should not be paid.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes the purpose of Chapter 15?
options: To establish monetary benefits, other than salary, payable under specified circumstances.
questions.explanation: Chapter 15 provides for various monetary benefits, distinct from salary, payable under prescribed conditions.

questions.question: A Ministry introduces a new allowance without Government approval or an Establishments Circular. According to Chapter 15, this action is:
options: Proper with the Permanent Secretary's approval.
Inconsistent with the Public Service Rules.
questions.explanation: Allowances payable in the Public Service are those prescribed by the Rules and relevant Government Circulars.

questions.question: An officer transferred officially to another duty station is entitled only to benefits specifically:
options: Authorized under the Public Service Rules.
questions.explanation: Transfer-related allowances are governed by the provisions of Chapter 15 and applicable Government approvals.

questions.question: A Government driver has maintained an accident-free record throughout the qualifying year, and the transport officer issues the prescribed certificate. The driver is entitled to:
questions.explanation: The Non-Accident Bonus is payable to eligible drivers upon presentation of the prescribed certificate confirming an accident-free record.

questions.question: Which allowance is specifically intended to compensate officers for expenses arising from official relocation?
questions.explanation: Resettlement Allowance assists officers with relocation expenses resulting from approved transfers.

questions.question: An officer is nominated for an official assignment to a cold-climate country but received Warm Clothing Allowance two years earlier. Under the Rules, the officer should ordinarily:
options: Receive another full Warm Clothing Allowance.
Wait until the prescribed three-year interval has elapsed before qualifying again.
questions.explanation: Warm Clothing Allowance is ordinarily payable once every three years.

questions.question: The overall objective of Chapter 15 is to ensure that officers receive:
options: Appropriate allowances under clearly defined conditions while promoting accountability in the use of public funds.
Equal allowances irrespective of official responsibility.
questions.explanation: Chapter 15 establishes the categories, conditions and administration of allowances payable to officers while ensuring proper control over public expenditure. Questions 911–920 Chapter 15 – Allowances (Part 5: Comprehensive Review & Application) Coverage: Comprehensive review of Chapter 15 – Allowances (Rules 150101–150507).

questions.question: Which allowance is specifically intended to compensate an officer for expenses arising from an official transfer that are not otherwise reimbursable?
questions.explanation: Resettlement Allowance is designed to offset expenses arising from an approved transfer that are not covered by other regulations.

questions.question: A Government driver has maintained an accident-free record throughout the year but forgets to obtain the prescribed Non-Accident Bonus Certificate before submitting a claim. According to the Rules, payment should:
options: Be made after obtaining the prescribed certificate.
Be replaced with Duty Tour Allowance.
Be doubled because of the clean record.
questions.explanation: Payment of the Non-Accident Bonus is based on the prescribed certificate issued by the appropriate transport authority.

questions.question: The purpose of Duty Tour Allowance is to cover:
options: Feeding and accommodation during approved official tours.
questions.explanation: Duty Tour Allowance assists officers with feeding and accommodation expenses incurred during approved official assignments.

questions.question: An officer is transferred at the officer's own request for personal reasons and applies for both Transport Allowance and Resettlement Allowance. Which benefit is payable?
questions.explanation: Officers transferred at their own request are entitled only to Transport Allowance and not Resettlement Allowance.

questions.question: The rates for Rent Allowance, Utility Allowance, Entertainment Allowance and similar allowances are:
options: Fixed permanently in the Public Service Rules.
Prescribed through relevant Government Circulars and reviewed periodically.
questions.explanation: These allowances are governed by Government Circulars and are reviewed periodically, generally every five years.

questions.question: An officer is nominated for an approved overseas course in a cold-climate country four years after previously receiving Warm Clothing Allowance. The officer is:
options: Eligible for another Warm Clothing Allowance.
Not eligible because the allowance is paid only once.
Required to refund the previous allowance first.
questions.explanation: Since more than the prescribed three-year interval has elapsed, the officer may qualify again for Warm Clothing Allowance.

questions.question: Wardrobe Allowance is calculated as:
options: A percentage of the officer's annual basic salary.
questions.explanation: Wardrobe Allowance is fixed at 10% of annual basic salary, payable once yearly.

questions.question: A Ministry proposes introducing a "Digital Communication Allowance" without any amendment to the Rules or issuance of a Government Circular. According to Chapter 15, this proposal:
options: May be implemented only if approved internally.
Requires proper Government authorization through the prescribed process.
Automatically becomes part of officers' salaries.
questions.explanation: New allowances or revisions to existing ones require proper Government authorization and are implemented through the prescribed regulatory framework.

questions.question: Which statement best reflects the administration of allowances under Chapter 15?
options: Every officer receives all listed allowances.
Allowances are payable only where the prescribed eligibility conditions are satisfied.
Allowances are determined by an officer's preference.
questions.explanation: Eligibility for each allowance depends on the specific conditions laid down in the Public Service Rules and relevant Government Circulars.

questions.question: A Human Resource Officer is explaining why Chapter 15 contains many different allowances instead of one general allowance. Which explanation best reflects the Rules?
options: Different allowances exist because they compensate for different official duties, responsibilities, and service conditions.
Every allowance is a reward for long service.
Allowances are intended to replace promotions.
questions.explanation: Chapter 15 recognizes that officers incur different official expenses and responsibilities, so separate allowances are provided for specific circumstances rather than a single general allowance. Questions 921–930 Chapter 16 – Inventions Coverage: Rules 160101–160205 – Official Inventions, Patents, Ownership, Awards and Secrecy.

questions.question: An invention made by an officer in the course of official duties shall ordinarily belong to:
options: The Ministry where the officer works
questions.explanation: Where an invention arises in the course of official duties, the rights belong to Government unless otherwise provided.

questions.question: Before applying for patent rights over an invention connected with official duties, an officer should first:
options: Obtain Government approval through the prescribed procedure.
questions.explanation: Officers are required to comply with Government procedures before seeking patent protection for official inventions.

questions.question: A Government engineer develops a surveying device using Government facilities during official working hours. The invention is regarded as:
questions.explanation: An invention produced in the course of official duty using Government resources belongs to Government.

questions.question: An officer whose invention benefits Government may receive:
options: Recognition or an award as approved by Government.
questions.explanation: The Rules provide for appropriate recognition or awards where an invention benefits Government.

questions.question: Information relating to an official invention should be treated as:
questions.explanation: Officers must preserve confidentiality regarding official inventions until disclosure is authorized.

questions.question: An officer discloses details of an official invention to a private company without approval. The officer has:
questions.explanation: Unauthorized disclosure of official inventions violates the provisions governing confidentiality.

questions.question: The objective of Chapter 16 is primarily to:
options: Encourage innovation while protecting Government interests.
questions.explanation: Chapter 16 balances encouragement of innovation with protection of Government ownership and interests.

questions.question: Government may seek patent protection for:
questions.explanation: Government may secure patent protection for inventions arising from official duties.

questions.question: An officer who develops an invention outside official duties and without Government resources:
options: May retain personal rights, subject to the Rules.
questions.explanation: The Rules distinguish between inventions connected with official duties and those developed independently.

questions.question: The overall purpose of Chapter 16 is to ensure that:
options: Valuable inventions are properly managed in the public interest.
questions.explanation: Chapter 16 establishes a framework for managing official inventions for the benefit of Government and the public. Questions 931–940 Chapter 17 – Reward for Outstanding Performance Coverage: Rules 170101–170104.

questions.question: The principal objective of Chapter 17 is to:
options: Reward exceptional performance in the Public Service.
questions.explanation: Chapter 17 establishes recognition for officers who demonstrate outstanding performance.

questions.question: Outstanding performance should primarily be rewarded to:
options: Encourage excellence and improve service delivery.
questions.explanation: Recognition encourages excellence and motivates officers toward higher productivity.

questions.question: An officer introduces a reform that significantly improves public service efficiency. Under Chapter 17, the officer may receive:
questions.explanation: Exceptional contributions may qualify an officer for official recognition or reward.

questions.question: Recognition under Chapter 17 is based principally on:
questions.explanation: Merit and exceptional performance form the basis for recognition.

questions.question: Awards under Chapter 17 are intended to:
questions.explanation: The reward system promotes excellence and improved public service performance.

questions.question: Two officers perform similar duties, but one consistently exceeds performance targets through innovation. The Rules support:
questions.explanation: Chapter 17 emphasizes merit-based recognition.

questions.question: Which principle best summarizes Chapter 17?
options: Reward should depend only on Grade Level.
Reward should depend only on years of service.
questions.explanation: Recognition is intended for officers who distinguish themselves through outstanding performance.

questions.question: Outstanding performance contributes directly to:
questions.explanation: Rewarding excellence encourages improved service delivery across Government.

questions.question: The reward system established in Chapter 17 is intended primarily to:
questions.explanation: Recognition serves as motivation for higher productivity and commitment.

questions.question: The overall philosophy of Chapter 17 is that:
questions.explanation: The chapter promotes a merit-based culture of excellence in the Public Service. Questions 951–960 Chapter 18 – Application of PSR to State Government Parastatals (Integrated Review) Coverage: Rules 180101–180306 – Recruitment, Promotion, Discipline, Boards, Appeals and General Administration of State Government Parastatals.

questions.question: Promotion in a State Government Parastatal should primarily be based on:
questions.explanation: Promotion within State Government Parastatals should follow approved procedures and be based principally on merit and other prescribed criteria under the applicable laws and regulations.

questions.question: A Governing Board of a State Government Parastatal approves a policy outside the powers granted by its enabling law. According to Chapter 18, the Board has acted:
options: Under the authority of the Civil Service Commission.
questions.explanation: Governing Boards must exercise only the powers conferred on them by their enabling legislation. Actions taken beyond those powers are inconsistent with the legal framework governing the Parastatal.

questions.question: The disciplinary procedures established for officers of State Government Parastatals are intended primarily to:
options: Ensure fairness and due process for both Government and employees.
questions.explanation: Chapter 18 emphasizes fair disciplinary procedures that observe due process while protecting the interests of both Government and employees.

questions.question: A newly established State Government Parastatal decides to recruit staff without advertising vacancies or applying approved recruitment procedures. This action is:
options: Permissible during the first year of operation.
Inconsistent with the recruitment principles established by the Rules.
Valid if approved by the Board Chairman alone.
questions.explanation: Recruitment into State Government Parastatals should comply with approved procedures that promote transparency, fairness and merit.

questions.question: An employee of a State Government Parastatal who is dissatisfied with an administrative decision should ordinarily:
options: Publish the complaint in the media.
Follow the approved petition and appeal procedures.
questions.explanation: Chapter 18 requires officers to use the established administrative procedures for petitions and appeals before pursuing other remedies.

questions.question: Which principle best promotes public confidence in the administration of State Government Parastatals?
questions.explanation: Effective administration of State Government Parastatals depends on accountability, fairness and transparency in decision-making.

questions.question: A Governing Board performs functions that are not authorized by its enabling law. In administrative law, this action is best described as:
questions.explanation: A Board acts ultra vires when it exercises powers beyond those granted by its enabling legislation, contrary to the principles governing State Government Parastatals.

questions.question: Performance management within State Government Parastatals should ultimately support:
options: Efficient and effective public service delivery.
questions.explanation: The administration of State Government Parastatals is intended to promote efficiency, accountability and improved service delivery.

questions.question: An employee immediately files a lawsuit against a State Government Parastatal without first utilizing the internal appeal procedures provided under the applicable regulations. According to Chapter 18, the employee should ordinarily have:
options: Exhausted the established administrative appeal procedures first.
Reported the matter to the media.
questions.explanation: The Rules encourage employees to utilize the prescribed internal petition and appeal mechanisms before seeking external remedies.

questions.question: The overall objective of Chapter 18 is to ensure that State Government Parastatals are administered:
options: Solely according to the decisions of their Boards.
In accordance with their enabling laws and the applicable principles of the Public Service Rules.
Only under the supervision of the Civil Service Commission.
questions.explanation: Chapter 18 provides that the administration of State Government Parastatals should be guided by their enabling laws together with the applicable principles of the Public Service Rules, ensuring legality, accountability and effective governance.

questions.question: An acting appointment is primarily made to:
options: Reward an officer for long service.
Enable an officer temporarily perform the duties of a higher office.
questions.explanation: Acting appointments enable officers to perform the duties of higher offices on a temporary basis.

questions.question: An acting appointment should ordinarily be made when:
options: A higher office becomes temporarily vacant or its substantive holder is unavailable.
questions.explanation: Acting appointments fill temporary vacancies or periods when the substantive holder cannot perform the duties.

questions.question: An officer is directed to perform the duties of a higher office for an approved period. The appointment is best described as:
questions.explanation: Performing the duties of a higher office temporarily constitutes an acting appointment.

questions.question: An acting appointment:
options: Is temporary and does not by itself amount to substantive promotion.
questions.explanation: Acting appointments are temporary and are distinct from substantive appointments or promotions.

questions.question: An officer on an approved acting appointment may become eligible for:
questions.explanation: Eligible officers serving in acting capacities may receive Acting Allowance in accordance with the Rules.

questions.question: An officer assumes the duties of a higher office without formal approval and claims Acting Allowance. The claim should be:
options: Declined because there was no approved acting appointment.
questions.explanation: Acting Allowance depends on a properly authorized acting appointment.

questions.question: The payment of Acting Allowance is governed by:
options: The provisions of the Public Service Rules and applicable Government approvals.
questions.explanation: Acting Allowances are paid only under the conditions prescribed by the Rules.

questions.question: An acting appointment normally ends when:
options: The substantive holder resumes duty or the appointment is otherwise terminated.
questions.explanation: Acting appointments continue only for the approved temporary period.

questions.question: A Ministry intends to use acting appointments to permanently avoid filling substantive vacancies. This practice is:
options: Consistent with the purpose of Chapter 19.
Inconsistent with the temporary nature of acting appointments.
questions.explanation: Acting appointments are temporary measures and are not substitutes for substantive appointments.

questions.question: The principal objective of Chapter 19 is to ensure:
options: Temporary continuity of administration where necessary.
questions.explanation: Acting appointments ensure uninterrupted administration during temporary vacancies.

questions.question: Overtime is work performed:
options: Beyond the approved normal working hours.
questions.explanation: Overtime refers to work performed beyond an officer's officially prescribed normal working hours.

questions.question: Payment for overtime is made only where:
questions.explanation: Overtime payment is not automatic. It is payable only where the additional work has been properly authorized by the appropriate authority in accordance with Government regulations and the Public Service Rules.

questions.question: An officer remains in the office after closing time to complete personal work and claims overtime. The claim should be:
questions.explanation: Overtime must relate to official duties carried out with proper authorization.

questions.question: Overtime should primarily be authorized where:
options: The exigencies of the service require additional work.
questions.explanation: The purpose of overtime is to meet genuine operational requirements where official duties cannot reasonably be completed within normal working hours.

questions.question: Overtime rates are prescribed by:
questions.explanation: The rates payable for overtime are prescribed by Government through approved regulations and relevant circulars.

questions.question: A supervisor authorizes overtime for duties that could reasonably have been completed during normal working hours without justification. This is:
questions.explanation: Supervisors should authorize overtime only where it is genuinely necessary.

questions.question: The purpose of overtime provisions is to:
options: Compensate eligible officers for authorized work beyond normal hours.

questions.question: Proper overtime administration requires:
questions.explanation: Proper administration of overtime requires accurate and verifiable records showing the work performed, the period worked, the approving authority and other relevant details before payment is processed.

questions.question: An officer falsifies overtime records to receive additional payment. This constitutes:
questions.explanation: Falsifying overtime records or claiming payment for work not performed constitutes financial misconduct. Such conduct undermines accountability and may attract disciplinary action under the Public Service Rules.

questions.question: Overtime claims should be:
questions.explanation: Before overtime claims are paid, they should be carefully verified to ensure that the work was actually performed, properly authorized, accurately recorded and eligible for payment under the Public Service Rules.

questions.question: The principal purpose of overtime payment under the Public Service Rules is to:
options: Increase the basic salary of officers.
Compensate eligible officers for properly authorized work performed beyond normal working hours.
Encourage officers to remain in the office after work.
questions.explanation: Overtime is intended to compensate officers for officially authorized work performed outside normal working hours.

questions.question: An officer who performs overtime without prior authorization is:
options: Not ordinarily entitled to overtime payment.
Entitled to Duty Tour Allowance instead.
questions.explanation: Overtime must be properly authorized before payment can be made.

questions.question: A supervisor discovers that overtime has been repeatedly approved for duties that could have been completed during normal office hours. According to the Rules, the supervisor should conclude that:
options: The overtime has been properly managed.
The overtime should automatically be converted into Acting Allowance.
questions.explanation: Overtime should be authorized only where the exigencies of the service genuinely require work beyond normal hours.

questions.question: For overtime claims to be processed correctly, records should be:
options: Prepared only at the end of the financial year.
questions.explanation: Proper documentation and verifiable records are essential before overtime claims are approved for payment.

questions.question: Overtime should ordinarily arise because:
options: Government offices remain open at night.
The exigencies of the service require work beyond normal working hours.
questions.explanation: The Rules provide that overtime should result from genuine service requirements rather than personal convenience.

questions.question: The rates payable for overtime are determined by:
questions.explanation: Overtime rates are prescribed through Government regulations and relevant circulars.

questions.question: An officer deliberately inflates the number of overtime hours worked in order to receive additional payment. This conduct constitutes:
questions.explanation: Fraudulent overtime claims amount to financial misconduct and undermine accountability in the Public Service.

questions.question: Before approving overtime, a supervisor should ensure that:
options: The work was necessary and properly authorized.
The officer requests payment in writing.
The work was performed during annual leave.
questions.explanation: Supervisors should authorize overtime only where it is justified by official duties and service needs.

questions.question: Which statement best summarizes the objective of Chapter 20?
options: To discourage officers from working after hours.
To ensure fair compensation for authorized overtime while safeguarding prudent use of public funds.
questions.explanation: Chapter 20 seeks to balance fair compensation with accountability and prudent financial management.

questions.question: A Director is briefing newly appointed officers on the philosophy behind the overtime provisions in the Public Service Rules. Which statement best reflects Chapter 20?
options: Every officer should work overtime to improve productivity.
Overtime is intended primarily as a salary enhancement scheme.
Overtime should be authorized only where necessary for efficient service delivery, and eligible officers should receive fair compensation for approved extra work.
Overtime replaces other allowances whenever officers work beyond office hours.
questions.explanation: The overall objective of Chapter 20 is to support efficient service delivery while ensuring that officers who perform properly authorized work beyond normal hours are fairly compensated.
